## Overview
Every EDGE element shares a common set of layout, styling, and event attributes. These are inherited from the base
`Element` class and can be applied to any native component -- containers, text, buttons, images, and more.
This page documents the shared attribute system that powers the layout engine across all EDGE elements.
## Sizing
Control element dimensions with width, height, and fill attributes.
```blade static
{{-- Fixed dimensions (in dp) --}}
<native:column :width="200" :height="100">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Fill available space --}}
<native:column fill-width>
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Fill both axes --}}
<native:column fill>
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Percentage width --}}
<native:column width="50%">
    ...
</native:column>
```
- `width` - Width in dp (float) or percentage string (e.g. `"50%"`)
- `height` - Height in dp (float) or percentage string
- `fill` - Fill both width and height of parent (boolean)
- `fill-width` - Fill parent width (boolean)
- `fill-height` - Fill parent height (boolean)
- `min-width` - Minimum width in dp (float)
- `max-width` - Maximum width in dp (float)
- `min-height` - Minimum height in dp (float)
- `max-height` - Maximum height in dp (float)
- `aspect-ratio` - Width-to-height ratio (float, e.g. `1.0` for square)
## Spacing
Padding and margin follow CSS shorthand conventions. Pass a single value for uniform spacing, or an array for
per-side control.
```blade static
{{-- Uniform padding --}}
<native:column :padding="16">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Vertical | Horizontal --}}
<native:column :padding="[12, 16]">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Top | Right | Bottom | Left --}}
<native:column :padding="[8, 16, 24, 16]">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Uniform margin --}}
<native:column :margin="8">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Gap between children --}}
<native:column :gap="12">
    ...
</native:column>
```
- `padding` - Inner spacing. Single value (float) or array of 2-4 values
- `margin` - Outer spacing. Single value (float) or array of 2-4 values
- `gap` - Space between children in dp (float)
## Flex Layout
The layout engine uses a Flexbox-based system. Containers (column, row) arrange children along a main axis, and flex
properties control how children grow, shrink, and align.
```blade static
{{-- Grow to fill remaining space --}}
<native:column :flex-grow="1">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Prevent shrinking --}}
<native:row :flex-shrink="0">
    ...
</native:row>
```
- `flex-grow` - How much this element grows relative to siblings (float, default: `0`)
- `flex-shrink` - How much this element shrinks when space is limited (float)
- `flex-basis` - Initial size before flex distribution (float or string)
<aside>
The Tailwind `flex-1` class is shorthand for `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: 0` — the most common pattern
for "fill the remaining space along the parent's main axis."
</aside>
## Alignment
Alignment attributes accept a **readable label**, a backing **enum**, or the raw **integer** — all three resolve to
the same value the native layout reads. Labels read best in Blade; enums give you autocomplete and type-safety when
building elements fluently in PHP.
```blade static
{{-- Center children on both axes --}}
<native:column center>
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Cross-axis alignment (horizontal in a column) --}}
<native:column align-items="center">
    <native:text>Centered text</native:text>
</native:column>
{{-- Main-axis distribution --}}
<native:row justify-content="space-between">
    <native:text>Left</native:text>
    <native:text>Right</native:text>
</native:row>
```
- `align-items` - Cross-axis alignment for children — `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`
- `justify-content` - Main-axis distribution — `start`, `center`, `end`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly`
- `align-self` - Override the parent's `align-items` for this element — `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`
- `center` - Shorthand: sets both `align-items` and `justify-content` to center (boolean)
### Underlying values
Labels map to these integers, which still work if you prefer them (`align-items="1"`):
| Integer | `align-items` / `align-self` | `justify-content` |
|---------|------------------------------|-------------------|
| `0` | *unset* — see below | start |
| `1` | center | center |
| `2` | end | end |
| `3` | stretch | space-between |
| `4` | start | space-around |
| `5` | — | space-evenly |
<aside>
For `align-items` and `align-self`, `0` means **unset** — not `start`. Start is `4`.
The renderers have to tell an element that explicitly asked for `items-start` apart from one that never specified
an alignment at all, because the two mean different things. Sharing a value made the first impossible to fix
without changing the second for every element in every app.
Passing `align-items="0"` therefore resolves to nothing and leaves the platform default in place. Use the label
(`align-items="start"`) or the enum rather than the integer — they are unambiguous.
</aside>
### In PHP
When you build elements fluently, pass a label, an enum case, or an integer. The enums live in
`Native\Mobile\Edge\Enums` — `AlignItems`, `AlignSelf`, `JustifyContent`, and `TextAlign`:
```php
use Native\Mobile\Edge\Elements\Column;
use Native\Mobile\Edge\Enums\AlignItems;
Column::make()
    ->alignItems(AlignItems::Center)     // enum — autocompletes, type-checked
    ->justifyContent('space-between');   // label string — also fine
```
<aside>
A child with `w-full` (or `h-full`) overrides its parent's `items-center` along that axis — same semantics as CSS
`align-self: stretch`. This is the easiest way to make one row in a centered column span the full width.
</aside>
## Style
Visual styling attributes that apply to any element.
```blade static
<native:column
    bg="#F0F0FF"
    :border-radius="12"
    :border-width="1"
    border-color="#E2E8F0"
    :opacity="0.9"
    :elevation="4"
>
    ...
</native:column>
```
- `bg` - Background color as hex string (e.g. `"#FF0000"`, `"#80FF000080"` for alpha)
- `border-radius` - Corner rounding in dp (float). Applies to all four corners — for per-side or per-corner
  rounding, use the `rounded-*` classes below
- `border-width` - Border width in dp (float). Must be used together with `border-color`
- `border-color` - Border color as hex string. Must be used together with `border-width`
- `opacity` - Element opacity from 0.0 to 1.0 (float)
- `elevation` - Shadow depth (float). Maps to platform shadow/elevation
## Events
Any element can respond to tap, double-tap, and long-press gestures. Use `@press`, `@doubleTap`, and `@longPress`
directives to bind methods on the route's PHP component class.
```blade static
<native:column @press="handleTap" @doubleTap="handleDoubleTap" @longPress="handleLongPress">
    <native:text>Tap, double tap, or long press me</native:text>
</native:column>
```
- `@press` - PHP method to call on tap
- `@doubleTap` - PHP method to call on double tap
- `@longPress` - PHP method to call on long press
## Safe Area
Respect the device's safe area insets (notch, home indicator, status bar) by adding the `safe-area` attribute. This is
typically applied to your outermost column.
```blade static
<native:column fill safe-area>
    {{-- Content will not overlap the notch or home indicator --}}
</native:column>
```
- `safe-area` - Inset content on both top and bottom edges (boolean)
- `safe-area-top` - Inset only the top edge (status bar / notch)
- `safe-area-bottom` - Inset only the bottom edge (home indicator)
See [Safe Area](../the-basics/safe-area) for the full picture, including how the framework's [layout](../the-basics/layouts)
chrome already handles safe-area insets for you.
## Visibility
Hide elements without removing them from the tree. A hidden element takes up no space in its parent's layout.
```blade static
<native:column hidden>
    {{-- This element is not displayed --}}
</native:column>
{{-- Bind it to component state --}}
<native:column :hidden="$collapsed">
    ...
</native:column>
```
- `hidden` - Hide this element (boolean). Takes precedence over any display class
The `hidden` class does the same job, and `flex` (or `block`) shows the element again. Pair them with a
[breakpoint](#responsive-breakpoints) to show something only on wider windows:
```blade static
{{-- A sidebar that only appears from tablet width up --}}
<native:column class="hidden md:flex w-[280] p-4 bg-theme-surface">
    ...
</native:column>
```
## Dark Mode
Override styles for dark mode using the `dark:` prefix with Tailwind classes, or pass a `dark` attribute array.
```blade static
{{-- Tailwind dark mode --}}
<native:column class="bg-white dark:bg-slate-900">
    <native:text class="text-black dark:text-white">
        Adapts to dark mode
    </native:text>
</native:column>
```
Dark mode overrides currently support `bg`, `color`, `border-color`, `opacity`, and `font-size`.
## Responsive Breakpoints
<x-docs.version-badge since="4.5" />
Prefix a class with a breakpoint to apply it only when the window is at least that wide. Breakpoints are
mobile-first, exactly as in Tailwind: an unprefixed class applies at every width, and `md:flex-row` takes over from
768 up.
```blade static
{{-- Stacked on a phone, side by side on a tablet --}}
<native:column class="w-full gap-6 p-4 md:flex-row md:gap-8 lg:p-8">
    <native:column class="md:flex-1">
        <native:text class="text-3xl md:text-5xl font-bold">Your jobs</native:text>
    </native:column>
    <native:column class="md:flex-1">
        ...
    </native:column>
</native:column>
```
| Prefix | Applies from |
|--------|--------------|
| `sm:` | 640 |
| `medium:` | 600 |
| `md:` | 768 |
| `expanded:` | 840 |
| `lg:` | 1024 |
| `xl:` | 1280 |
| `2xl:` | 1536 |
Widths are points on iOS and dp on Android. `sm:` to `2xl:` are Tailwind's breakpoints; `medium:` and `expanded:`
follow the medium and expanded window size classes in Material Design, if you'd rather design to those.
Breakpoints are measured against the app's **window**, not the device's screen, and resolved on the device. The same
screen re-flows as soon as the window changes width, whether the device rotates or the app is resized in Split View,
without a round trip to PHP. An iPad in portrait and in landscape can land on different breakpoints.
Each breakpoint builds on everything narrower. Only the classes you prefix change, so `p-4 md:px-8` keeps its
vertical padding at `md`, and `rounded-xl md:rounded-t-3xl` keeps its rounded bottom corners.
Any class from the [supported classes](#supported-tailwind-classes) can take a breakpoint prefix, except
`whitespace-*`, which is applied to text content before it reaches the device. Breakpoints combine with the other
variants in either order, so `md:dark:bg-zinc-900`, `dark:md:bg-zinc-900` and `ios:md:p-6` all work.
### Customizing breakpoints
The thresholds live in `config/nativephp.php`. Change a width, remove the breakpoints you don't use, or add your
own names:
```php
'breakpoints' => [
    'sm' => 640,
    'md' => 768,
    'tablet' => 700, // enables `tablet:` classes
    'lg' => 1024,
],
```
The table replaces the defaults entirely, so keep every name you still use in your views. If the key is missing or
empty, the defaults above apply.
<aside>
Breakpoints are min-width only. Tailwind's `max-*:` range variants (`max-md:hidden`) and arbitrary breakpoints
(`min-[900px]:`) are not supported and are dropped. Write the mobile-first form instead: `flex md:hidden` rather
than `max-md:flex`.
</aside>
## Tailwind Classes
EDGE includes a built-in Tailwind CSS parser that converts familiar utility classes into native layout attributes. Use
the `class` attribute on any element.
```blade static
<native:column class="w-full p-4 gap-3 bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md items-center">
    <native:text class="text-2xl font-bold text-slate-900">
        Styled with Tailwind
    </native:text>
</native:column>
```
### Supported Tailwind classes
The parser recognizes the classes listed below.
| Category | Classes |
|----------|---------|
| Width | `w-full`, `w-N`, fractional (`w-1/2`, `w-1/3`, `w-2/3`, `w-1/4`, `w-3/4`, `w-1/5`…), arbitrary `w-[N]` |
| Height | `h-full`, `h-N`, arbitrary `h-[N]` |
| Min / max size | `min-w-N`, `max-w-N`, `min-h-N`, `max-h-N`, `max-w-none`, the container scale on `max-w` (`max-w-xs` … `max-w-7xl`), arbitrary `max-w-[N]` etc. |

| Grid columns <x-docs.version-badge since="4.5" /> | `grid-cols-N` — sets the column count of a [lazy grid](lazy-grid) |
| Items (cross-axis) | `items-start`, `items-center`, `items-end`, `items-stretch` |
| Justify (main-axis) | `justify-start`, `justify-center`, `justify-end`, `justify-between`, `justify-around`, `justify-evenly` |
| Self | `self-start`, `self-center`, `self-end`, `self-stretch` |

```blade static
{{-- Fixed dimensions (in dp) --}}
<native:column :width="200" :height="100">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Fill available space --}}
<native:column fill-width>
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Fill both axes --}}
<native:column fill>
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Percentage width --}}
<native:column width="50%">
    ...
</native:column>
```
- `width` - Width in dp (float) or percentage string (e.g. `"50%"`)
- `height` - Height in dp (float) or percentage string
- `fill` - Fill both width and height of parent (boolean)
- `fill-width` - Fill parent width (boolean)
- `fill-height` - Fill parent height (boolean)
- `min-width` - Minimum width in dp (float)
- `max-width` - Maximum width in dp (float)
- `min-height` - Minimum height in dp (float)
- `max-height` - Maximum height in dp (float)
- `aspect-ratio` - Width-to-height ratio (float, e.g. `1.0` for square)
## Spacing
Padding and margin follow CSS shorthand conventions. Pass a single value for uniform spacing, or an array for
per-side control.
```blade static
{{-- Uniform padding --}}
<native:column :padding="16">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Vertical | Horizontal --}}
<native:column :padding="[12, 16]">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Top | Right | Bottom | Left --}}
<native:column :padding="[8, 16, 24, 16]">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Uniform margin --}}
<native:column :margin="8">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Gap between children --}}
<native:column :gap="12">
    ...
</native:column>
```
- `padding` - Inner spacing. Single value (float) or array of 2-4 values
- `margin` - Outer spacing. Single value (float) or array of 2-4 values
- `gap` - Space between children in dp (float)
## Flex Layout
The layout engine uses a Flexbox-based system. Containers (column, row) arrange children along a main axis, and flex
properties control how children grow, shrink, and align.
```blade static
{{-- Grow to fill remaining space --}}
<native:column :flex-grow="1">
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Prevent shrinking --}}
<native:row :flex-shrink="0">
    ...
</native:row>
```
- `flex-grow` - How much this element grows relative to siblings (float, default: `0`)
- `flex-shrink` - How much this element shrinks when space is limited (float)
- `flex-basis` - Initial size before flex distribution (float or string)
<aside>
The Tailwind `flex-1` class is shorthand for `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: 0` — the most common pattern
for "fill the remaining space along the parent's main axis."
</aside>
## Alignment
Alignment attributes accept a **readable label**, a backing **enum**, or the raw **integer** — all three resolve to
the same value the native layout reads. Labels read best in Blade; enums give you autocomplete and type-safety when
building elements fluently in PHP.
```blade static
{{-- Center children on both axes --}}
<native:column center>
    ...
</native:column>
{{-- Cross-axis alignment (horizontal in a column) --}}
<native:column align-items="center">
    <native:text>Centered text</native:text>
</native:column>
{{-- Main-axis distribution --}}
<native:row justify-content="space-between">
    <native:text>Left</native:text>
    <native:text>Right</native:text>
</native:row>
```
- `align-items` - Cross-axis alignment for children — `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`
- `justify-content` - Main-axis distribution — `start`, `center`, `end`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly`
- `align-self` - Override the parent's `align-items` for this element — `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`
- `center` - Shorthand: sets both `align-items` and `justify-content` to center (boolean)
### Underlying values
Labels map to these integers, which still work if you prefer them (`align-items="1"`):
| Integer | `align-items` / `align-self` | `justify-content` |
|---------|------------------------------|-------------------|
| `0` | *unset* — see below | start |
| `1` | center | center |
| `2` | end | end |
| `3` | stretch | space-between |
| `4` | start | space-around |
| `5` | — | space-evenly |
<aside>
For `align-items` and `align-self`, `0` means **unset** — not `start`. Start is `4`.
The renderers have to tell an element that explicitly asked for `items-start` apart from one that never specified
an alignment at all, because the two mean different things. Sharing a value made the first impossible to fix
without changing the second for every element in every app.
Passing `align-items="0"` therefore resolves to nothing and leaves the platform default in place. Use the label
(`align-items="start"`) or the enum rather than the integer — they are unambiguous.
</aside>
### In PHP
When you build elements fluently, pass a label, an enum case, or an integer. The enums live in
`Native\Mobile\Edge\Enums` — `AlignItems`, `AlignSelf`, `JustifyContent`, and `TextAlign`:
```php
use Native\Mobile\Edge\Elements\Column;
use Native\Mobile\Edge\Enums\AlignItems;
Column::make()
    ->alignItems(AlignItems::Center)     // enum — autocompletes, type-checked
    ->justifyContent('space-between');   // label string — also fine
```
<aside>
A child with `w-full` (or `h-full`) overrides its parent's `items-center` along that axis — same semantics as CSS
`align-self: stretch`. This is the easiest way to make one row in a centered column span the full width.
</aside>
## Style
Visual styling attributes that apply to any element.
```blade static
<native:column
    bg="#F0F0FF"
    :border-radius="12"
    :border-width="1"
    border-color="#E2E8F0"
    :opacity="0.9"
    :elevation="4"
>
    ...
</native:column>
```
- `bg` - Background color as hex string (e.g. `"#FF0000"`, `"#80FF000080"` for alpha)
- `border-radius` - Corner rounding in dp (float). Applies to all four corners — for per-side or per-corner
  rounding, use the `rounded-*` classes below
- `border-width` - Border width in dp (float). Must be used together with `border-color`
- `border-color` - Border color as hex string. Must be used together with `border-width`
- `opacity` - Element opacity from 0.0 to 1.0 (float)
- `elevation` - Shadow depth (float). Maps to platform shadow/elevation
## Events
Any element can respond to tap, double-tap, and long-press gestures. Use `@press`, `@doubleTap`, and `@longPress`
directives to bind methods on the route's PHP component class.
```blade static
<native:column @press="handleTap" @doubleTap="handleDoubleTap" @longPress="handleLongPress">
    <native:text>Tap, double tap, or long press me</native:text>
</native:column>
```
- `@press` - PHP method to call on tap
- `@doubleTap` - PHP method to call on double tap
- `@longPress` - PHP method to call on long press
## Safe Area
Respect the device's safe area insets (notch, home indicator, status bar) by adding the `safe-area` attribute. This is
typically applied to your outermost column.
```blade static
<native:column fill safe-area>
    {{-- Content will not overlap the notch or home indicator --}}
</native:column>
```
- `safe-area` - Inset content on both top and bottom edges (boolean)
- `safe-area-top` - Inset only the top edge (status bar / notch)
- `safe-area-bottom` - Inset only the bottom edge (home indicator)
See [Safe Area](../the-basics/safe-area) for the full picture, including how the framework's [layout](../the-basics/layouts)
chrome already handles safe-area insets for you.
## Visibility
Hide elements without removing them from the tree. A hidden element takes up no space in its parent's layout.
```blade static
<native:column hidden>
    {{-- This element is not displayed --}}
</native:column>
{{-- Bind it to component state --}}
<native:column :hidden="$collapsed">
    ...
</native:column>
```
- `hidden` - Hide this element (boolean). Takes precedence over any display class
The `hidden` class does the same job, and `flex` (or `block`) shows the element again. Pair them with a
[breakpoint](#responsive-breakpoints) to show something only on wider windows:
```blade static
{{-- A sidebar that only appears from tablet width up --}}
<native:column class="hidden md:flex w-[280] p-4 bg-theme-surface">
    ...
</native:column>
```
## Dark Mode
Override styles for dark mode using the `dark:` prefix with Tailwind classes, or pass a `dark` attribute array.
```blade static
{{-- Tailwind dark mode --}}
<native:column class="bg-white dark:bg-slate-900">
    <native:text class="text-black dark:text-white">
        Adapts to dark mode
    </native:text>
</native:column>
```
Dark mode overrides currently support `bg`, `color`, `border-color`, `opacity`, and `font-size`.
## Responsive Breakpoints
<x-docs.version-badge since="4.5" />
Prefix a class with a breakpoint to apply it only when the window is at least that wide. Breakpoints are
mobile-first, exactly as in Tailwind: an unprefixed class applies at every width, and `md:flex-row` takes over from
768 up.
```blade static
{{-- Stacked on a phone, side by side on a tablet --}}
<native:column class="w-full gap-6 p-4 md:flex-row md:gap-8 lg:p-8">
    <native:column class="md:flex-1">
        <native:text class="text-3xl md:text-5xl font-bold">Your jobs</native:text>
    </native:column>
    <native:column class="md:flex-1">
        ...
    </native:column>
</native:column>
```
| Prefix | Applies from |
|--------|--------------|
| `sm:` | 640 |
| `medium:` | 600 |
| `md:` | 768 |
| `expanded:` | 840 |
| `lg:` | 1024 |
| `xl:` | 1280 |
| `2xl:` | 1536 |
Widths are points on iOS and dp on Android. `sm:` to `2xl:` are Tailwind's breakpoints; `medium:` and `expanded:`
follow the medium and expanded window size classes in Material Design, if you'd rather design to those.
Breakpoints are measured against the app's **window**, not the device's screen, and resolved on the device. The same
screen re-flows as soon as the window changes width, whether the device rotates or the app is resized in Split View,
without a round trip to PHP. An iPad in portrait and in landscape can land on different breakpoints.
Each breakpoint builds on everything narrower. Only the classes you prefix change, so `p-4 md:px-8` keeps its
vertical padding at `md`, and `rounded-xl md:rounded-t-3xl` keeps its rounded bottom corners.
Any class from the [supported classes](#supported-tailwind-classes) can take a breakpoint prefix, except
`whitespace-*`, which is applied to text content before it reaches the device. Breakpoints combine with the other
variants in either order, so `md:dark:bg-zinc-900`, `dark:md:bg-zinc-900` and `ios:md:p-6` all work.
### Customizing breakpoints
The thresholds live in `config/nativephp.php`. Change a width, remove the breakpoints you don't use, or add your
own names:
```php
'breakpoints' => [
    'sm' => 640,
    'md' => 768,
    'tablet' => 700, // enables `tablet:` classes
    'lg' => 1024,
],
```
The table replaces the defaults entirely, so keep every name you still use in your views. If the key is missing or
empty, the defaults above apply.
<aside>
Breakpoints are min-width only. Tailwind's `max-*:` range variants (`max-md:hidden`) and arbitrary breakpoints
(`min-[900px]:`) are not supported and are dropped. Write the mobile-first form instead: `flex md:hidden` rather
than `max-md:flex`.
</aside>
## Tailwind Classes
EDGE includes a built-in Tailwind CSS parser that converts familiar utility classes into native layout attributes. Use
the `class` attribute on any element.
```blade static
<native:column class="w-full p-4 gap-3 bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md items-center">
    <native:text class="text-2xl font-bold text-slate-900">
        Styled with Tailwind
    </native:text>
</native:column>
```
### Supported Tailwind classes
The parser recognizes the classes listed below.
| Category | Classes |
|----------|---------|
| Width | `w-full`, `w-N`, fractional (`w-1/2`, `w-1/3`, `w-2/3`, `w-1/4`, `w-3/4`, `w-1/5`…), arbitrary `w-[N]` |
| Height | `h-full`, `h-N`, arbitrary `h-[N]` |
| Min / max size | `min-w-N`, `max-w-N`, `min-h-N`, `max-h-N`, `max-w-none`, the container scale on `max-w` (`max-w-xs` … `max-w-7xl`), arbitrary `max-w-[N]` etc. |
| Aspect ratio | `aspect-square`, `aspect-video`, arbitrary `aspect-[N]` |
| Object fit (images) | `object-contain`, `object-cover`, `object-fill`, `object-none`, `object-scale-down` |
| Padding | `p-N`, `px-N`, `py-N`, `pt-N`, `pr-N`, `pb-N`, `pl-N`, arbitrary `p-[N]` etc. |
| Margin | `m-N`, `mx-N`, `my-N`, `mt-N`, `mr-N`, `mb-N`, `ml-N`, arbitrary `m-[N]` etc. |
| Gap | `gap-N`, `gap-[N]` (uniform — no `gap-x-*` or `gap-y-*`) |
| Position | `absolute`, `relative`, `top-N`, `right-N`, `bottom-N`, `left-N`, arbitrary `top-[N]` etc. |
| Flex | `flex-1`, `flex-grow`, `flex-grow-0`, `flex-shrink`, `flex-shrink-0`, `flex-wrap`, `flex-nowrap`, `flex-wrap-reverse` |
| Display <x-docs.version-badge since="4.5" /> | `hidden`; `flex`, `inline-flex`, `block`, `inline-block` and `grid` show the element again (for `hidden md:flex`) |
| Grid columns <x-docs.version-badge since="4.5" /> | `grid-cols-N` — sets the column count of a [lazy grid](lazy-grid) |
| Items (cross-axis) | `items-start`, `items-center`, `items-end`, `items-stretch` |
| Justify (main-axis) | `justify-start`, `justify-center`, `justify-end`, `justify-between`, `justify-around`, `justify-evenly` |
| Self | `self-start`, `self-center`, `self-end`, `self-stretch` |
| Background | `bg-{palette}-{shade}` (e.g. `bg-red-500`), `bg-white`, `bg-black`, `bg-transparent`, `bg-[#hex]`, `bg-theme-{token}` |
| Text color | `text-{palette}-{shade}`, `text-white`, `text-black`, `text-transparent`, `text-[#hex]`, `text-theme-{token}` |
| Border color | `border-{palette}-{shade}`, `border-white`, `border-black`, `border-transparent`, `border-[#hex]`, `border-theme-{token}` |
| Border width | `border` (1dp), `border-2`, `border-4`, `border-8` |
| Border width (per side) <x-docs.version-badge since="4.7" /> | `border-t`, `border-r`, `border-b`, `border-l`, and `border-x` / `border-y` for two sides at once. Each takes the same `-0`, `-2`, `-4`, `-8` scale and arbitrary values (`border-l-[1.5]`). A bare side (`border-l`) is 1dp. See [Dashed, dotted and per-side borders](#dashed-dotted-and-per-side-borders) |
| Border style <x-docs.version-badge since="4.7" /> | `border-solid`, `border-dashed`, `border-dotted` |
| Rounded | `rounded` (4dp), `rounded-sm`, `rounded-md`, `rounded-lg`, `rounded-xl`, `rounded-2xl`, `rounded-3xl`, `rounded-full`, `rounded-[N]` |
| Rounded (per side) <x-docs.version-badge since="4.2" /> | `rounded-t-*`, `rounded-r-*`, `rounded-b-*`, `rounded-l-*` — each rounds that side's two corners. A bare side (`rounded-b`) uses the same 4dp default as `rounded` |
| Rounded (per corner) <x-docs.version-badge since="4.2" /> | `rounded-tl-*`, `rounded-tr-*`, `rounded-br-*`, `rounded-bl-*`, including arbitrary values (`rounded-br-[4]`) |
| Shadow | `shadow`, `shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, `shadow-lg`, `shadow-xl`, `shadow-2xl`, `shadow-inner`, `shadow-none` |
| Opacity | `opacity-{0..100}`, arbitrary `opacity-[0.5]` |
| Text size | `text-xs`, `text-sm`, `text-base`, `text-lg`, `text-xl`, `text-2xl`, `text-3xl`, `text-4xl`, `text-5xl`, `text-6xl`, `text-7xl`, `text-8xl`, `text-9xl`, arbitrary `text-[N]` |
| Font weight | `font-thin`, `font-extralight`, `font-light`, `font-normal`, `font-medium`, `font-semibold`, `font-bold`, `font-extrabold`, `font-black` |
| Font family | `font-sans`, `font-serif`, `font-mono` |
| Font style | `italic`, `not-italic` |
| Text decoration | `underline`, `line-through`, `no-underline` |
| Text transform | `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize`, `normal-case` |
| Letter spacing | `tracking-tighter`, `tracking-tight`, `tracking-normal`, `tracking-wide`, `tracking-wider`, `tracking-widest` |
| Line height | `leading-none`, `leading-tight`, `leading-snug`, `leading-normal`, `leading-relaxed`, `leading-loose`, arbitrary `leading-[1.4]` / `leading-[24px]` |
| Text align | `text-left`, `text-center`, `text-right` |
| Text selection | `select-text`, `select-none` (container-scoped; descendants inherit) |
| Safe area | `safe-area` (top + bottom), `safe-area-top`, `safe-area-bottom` |
| Liquid Glass | `glass`, `glass:prominent`, `glass:interactive`, `glass:clear` (compose: `glass:clear:interactive`) |
**Variants** — prepend any class:
| Prefix | Effect |
|----------|---------|
| `dark:` | Applies in dark mode (e.g. `dark:bg-zinc-900`) |
| `ios:` | Applies on iOS only — drops silently on Android |
| `android:` | Applies on Android only — drops silently on iOS |
| `sm:` `md:` `lg:` `xl:` `2xl:` | Applies from that window width up — see [Responsive Breakpoints](#responsive-breakpoints) |
Variants compose freely, in either order: `ios:dark:bg-zinc-800`, `dark:ios:bg-zinc-800` and `md:dark:bg-zinc-800`

plugins/bridge-functions.md:title: Bridge Functions
plugins/bridge-functions.md:order: 400
plugins/bridge-functions.md:---
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## How Bridge Functions Work
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Bridge functions are the connection between your PHP code and native platform code. When you call a method like
plugins/bridge-functions.md:`MyPlugin::doSomething()`, NativePHP routes that to your Swift or Kotlin implementation running on the device.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:The flow:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:1. PHP calls `nativephp_call('MyPlugin.DoSomething', $params)`
plugins/bridge-functions.md:2. The native bridge locates the registered function
plugins/bridge-functions.md:3. Your native code executes and returns a response
plugins/bridge-functions.md:4. PHP receives the result
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Declaring Bridge Functions
plugins/bridge-functions.md:In your `nativephp.json`, declare each function with its platform implementations:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```json
plugins/bridge-functions.md:{
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    "bridge_functions": [
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            "name": "MyPlugin.DoSomething",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            "ios": "MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            "android": "com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin.MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            "description": "Does something useful"
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    ]
plugins/bridge-functions.md:}
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:The `name` is what PHP uses. The platform-specific values point to your native class and method.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:### Naming Convention
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- **`name`** — A unique identifier like `MyPlugin.DoSomething`. This is what PHP code uses.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- **`ios`** — Swift enum/class path: `EnumName.ClassName`
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- **`android`** — Full Kotlin class path including your vendor package (e.g., `com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin.ClassName`)
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Swift Implementation (iOS)
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Create your functions in `resources/ios/Sources/`:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```swift
plugins/bridge-functions.md:import Foundation
plugins/bridge-functions.md:enum MyPluginFunctions {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    class DoSomething: BridgeFunction {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        func execute(parameters: [String: Any]) throws -> [String: Any] {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            let option = parameters["option"] as? String ?? ""
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            // Do your native work here
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            return BridgeResponse.success(data: [
plugins/bridge-functions.md:                "result": "completed",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:                "option": option
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            ])
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:}
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Key points:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- Implement the `BridgeFunction` protocol
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- Parameters come as a dictionary
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- Return using `BridgeResponse.success()` or `BridgeResponse.error()`
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Kotlin Implementation (Android)
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Create your functions in `resources/android/src/`. Use your own vendor-namespaced package:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```kotlin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:package com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:import com.nativephp.mobile.bridge.BridgeFunction
plugins/bridge-functions.md:import com.nativephp.mobile.bridge.BridgeResponse
plugins/bridge-functions.md:object MyPluginFunctions {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    class DoSomething : BridgeFunction {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        override fun execute(parameters: Map<String, Any>): Map<String, Any> {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            val option = parameters["option"] as? String ?: ""
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            // Do your native work here
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            return BridgeResponse.success(mapOf(
plugins/bridge-functions.md:                "result" to "completed",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:                "option" to option
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            ))
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:}
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:The package declaration determines where your file is placed during compilation. Using `com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin` ensures
plugins/bridge-functions.md:your code is isolated from other plugins and the core NativePHP code.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Calling from PHP
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Create a facade method that calls your bridge function:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```php
plugins/bridge-functions.md:class MyPlugin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:{
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    public function doSomething(array $options = []): mixed
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        if (function_exists('nativephp_call')) {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            $result = nativephp_call('MyPlugin.DoSomething', json_encode($options));
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            return json_decode($result)?->data;
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        return null;
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:}
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Error Handling
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Return errors from native code using `BridgeResponse.error()`:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```swift
plugins/bridge-functions.md:// Swift
plugins/bridge-functions.md:return BridgeResponse.error(message: "Something went wrong")
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```kotlin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:// Kotlin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:return BridgeResponse.error("Something went wrong")
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:The error message is available in PHP through the response.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Official Plugins & Dev Kit
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Need native functionality without writing Kotlin or Swift? Browse ready-made plugins or get the Dev Kit to build your own.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:[Visit the NativePHP Plugin Marketplace →](https://nativephp.com/plugins)

plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Scaffolding a Plugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The quickest way to create a plugin is with the interactive scaffolding command:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:create
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This walks you through naming, namespace selection, and feature options, then generates a complete plugin structure.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The first prompt asks which kind of plugin you're building. A **system plugin** adds native capabilities you call from
plugins/creating-plugins.md:PHP — the rest of this page. A **UI component plugin** adds new EDGE elements rendered by your own SwiftUI and Compose
plugins/creating-plugins.md:code; see [UI Component Plugins](./ui-components) for that path.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:<aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:#### Build Plugins 10x Faster
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Writing native Kotlin and Swift code is the hardest part of plugin development. The
plugins/creating-plugins.md:[NativePHP Plugin Development Kit](/products/plugin-dev-kit) for Claude Code can generate production-ready
plugins/creating-plugins.md:plugins in minutes — complete with bridge functions, events, permissions, and platform-specific implementations.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:[Get the Plugin Dev Kit →](/products/plugin-dev-kit)
plugins/creating-plugins.md:</aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Plugin Structure
plugins/creating-plugins.md:A plugin follows a standard layout:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:my-plugin/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:├── composer.json          # Package metadata, type must be "nativephp-plugin"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:├── nativephp.json         # Plugin manifest
plugins/creating-plugins.md:├── src/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── MyPluginServiceProvider.php
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── MyPlugin.php       # Main class
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── Facades/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   │   └── MyPlugin.php
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── Events/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   │   └── SomethingHappened.php
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   └── Commands/          # Lifecycle hook commands
plugins/creating-plugins.md:├── resources/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── android/src/       # Kotlin bridge functions
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── ios/Sources/       # Swift bridge functions
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   └── js/                # JavaScript library stubs
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Android Package Naming
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Android/Kotlin code must declare a package at the top of each file. Use your own vendor-namespaced package to avoid
plugins/creating-plugins.md:conflicts:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```kotlin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:// resources/android/src/MyPluginFunctions.kt
plugins/creating-plugins.md:package com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:import com.nativephp.mobile.bridge.BridgeFunction
plugins/creating-plugins.md:import com.nativephp.mobile.bridge.BridgeResponse
plugins/creating-plugins.md:object MyPluginFunctions {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    class DoSomething : BridgeFunction {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        override fun execute(parameters: Map<String, Any>): Map<String, Any> {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            return BridgeResponse.success(mapOf("status" to "done"))
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The compiler places files based on their package declaration, so `package com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin` results in the file
plugins/creating-plugins.md:being placed at `app/src/main/java/com/myvendor/plugins/myplugin/MyPluginFunctions.kt`.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:<aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Files without package declarations will be placed in a fallback location, but this is not recommended. Always declare
plugins/creating-plugins.md:packages in your Kotlin files.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:</aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Reference the full package path in your manifest's bridge functions:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "bridge_functions": [{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "name": "MyPlugin.DoSomething",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "android": "com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin.MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    }]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## The composer.json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Your `composer.json` must specify the plugin type:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "name": "vendor/my-plugin",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "type": "nativephp-plugin",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "extra": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "laravel": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "providers": ["Vendor\\MyPlugin\\MyPluginServiceProvider"]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        },
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "nativephp": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "manifest": "nativephp.json"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The `type: nativephp-plugin` tells NativePHP to look for native code in this package.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## The nativephp.json Manifest
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The manifest declares native-specific configuration for your plugin. Package metadata (`name`, `version`, `description`,
plugins/creating-plugins.md:`service_provider`) comes from your `composer.json` — don't duplicate it here.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "namespace": "MyPlugin",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "bridge_functions": [
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "name": "MyPlugin.DoSomething",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "ios": "MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "android": "com.nativephp.plugins.myplugin.MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    ],
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "events": ["Vendor\\MyPlugin\\Events\\SomethingHappened"],
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "android": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "permissions": ["android.permission.CAMERA"],
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "dependencies": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "implementation": ["com.google.mlkit:barcode-scanning:17.2.0"]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    },
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "ios": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "info_plist": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "NSCameraUsageDescription": "Camera is used for scanning"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        },
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "dependencies": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "pods": [{"name": "GoogleMLKit/BarcodeScanning", "version": "~> 4.0"}]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### Manifest Fields
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| Field | Required | Description |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:|-------|----------|-------------|
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `namespace` | Yes | Namespace for the plugin (used for code generation and directory structure) |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `bridge_functions` | No | Array of native function mappings |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `events` | No | Event classes the plugin dispatches |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.permissions` | No | Android permission strings |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.features` | No | Android uses-feature declarations |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.dependencies` | No | Gradle dependencies |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.repositories` | No | Custom Maven repositories |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.activities` | No | Activities to register in manifest |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.services` | No | Services to register in manifest |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.receivers` | No | Broadcast receivers to register |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.providers` | No | Content providers to register |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.meta_data` | No | Application meta-data entries |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.min_version` | No | Minimum Android SDK version required |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.init_function` | No | Native function to call during app initialization |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.info_plist` | No | Info.plist entries (permissions, API keys) |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.dependencies` | No | Swift packages and CocoaPods |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.background_modes` | No | UIBackgroundModes values |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.entitlements` | No | App entitlements |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.capabilities` | No | iOS capabilities for Xcode project |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.min_version` | No | Minimum iOS version required |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.init_function` | No | Native function to call during app initialization |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `assets` | No | Declarative asset copying |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `hooks` | No | Lifecycle hook commands |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `secrets` | No | Required environment variables |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:See [Advanced Configuration](advanced-configuration) for detailed documentation on each field.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Local Development
plugins/creating-plugins.md:During development, add your plugin to your app's `composer.json` as a path repository:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "repositories": [
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        {"type": "path", "url": "../packages/my-plugin"}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    ]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Then require it:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:composer require vendor/my-plugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Changes to your plugin's PHP code are picked up immediately. Changes to native code require a rebuild with
plugins/creating-plugins.md:`php artisan native:run`.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:When testing significant changes to your plugin's native code or manifest, you may need to force a fresh install of
plugins/creating-plugins.md:the native projects:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:install --force
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This ensures the native projects are rebuilt from scratch with your latest plugin configuration.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:<aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:#### Validate Early and Often
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Run `php artisan native:plugin:validate` to catch manifest errors, missing native code, or mismatched function
plugins/creating-plugins.md:declarations before you try to build.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:</aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Registering Plugins
plugins/creating-plugins.md:After installing a plugin with Composer, you need to register it so it gets compiled into your native builds.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### First Time Setup
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Publish the NativeServiceProvider:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan vendor:publish --tag=nativephp-plugins-provider
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This creates `app/Providers/NativeServiceProvider.php`.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### Register a Plugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:register vendor/plugin-name
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This automatically adds the plugin's service provider to your `plugins()` array:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```php
plugins/creating-plugins.md:public function plugins(): array
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    return [
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        \Vendor\PluginName\PluginNameServiceProvider::class,
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    ];
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### List Plugins
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:# Show registered plugins
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:list
plugins/creating-plugins.md:# Show all installed plugins (including unregistered)
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:list --all
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### Remove a Plugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:register vendor/plugin-name --remove
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:<aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This explicit registration is a security measure. It prevents transitive dependencies from automatically
plugins/creating-plugins.md:registering plugins without your consent.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:</aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## JavaScript Library
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Plugins can provide a JavaScript library for SPA frameworks. The scaffolding creates a stub in `resources/js/`:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```js
plugins/creating-plugins.md:// resources/js/myPlugin.js
plugins/creating-plugins.md:const baseUrl = '/_native/api/call';
plugins/creating-plugins.md:async function bridgeCall(method, params = {}) {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    const response = await fetch(baseUrl, {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        method: 'POST',
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        body: JSON.stringify({ method, params })
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    });
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    return response.json();
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:export async function doSomething(options = {}) {

plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Users can then import your functions directly in Vue, React, or vanilla JS.

plugins/bridge-functions.md:## How Bridge Functions Work
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Bridge functions are the connection between your PHP code and native platform code. When you call a method like
plugins/bridge-functions.md:`MyPlugin::doSomething()`, NativePHP routes that to your Swift or Kotlin implementation running on the device.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:The flow:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:1. PHP calls `nativephp_call('MyPlugin.DoSomething', $params)`
plugins/bridge-functions.md:2. The native bridge locates the registered function
plugins/bridge-functions.md:3. Your native code executes and returns a response
plugins/bridge-functions.md:4. PHP receives the result
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Declaring Bridge Functions
plugins/bridge-functions.md:In your `nativephp.json`, declare each function with its platform implementations:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```json
plugins/bridge-functions.md:{
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    "bridge_functions": [
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            "name": "MyPlugin.DoSomething",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            "ios": "MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            "android": "com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin.MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            "description": "Does something useful"
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    ]
plugins/bridge-functions.md:}
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:The `name` is what PHP uses. The platform-specific values point to your native class and method.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:### Naming Convention
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- **`name`** — A unique identifier like `MyPlugin.DoSomething`. This is what PHP code uses.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- **`ios`** — Swift enum/class path: `EnumName.ClassName`
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- **`android`** — Full Kotlin class path including your vendor package (e.g., `com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin.ClassName`)
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Swift Implementation (iOS)
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Create your functions in `resources/ios/Sources/`:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```swift
plugins/bridge-functions.md:import Foundation
plugins/bridge-functions.md:enum MyPluginFunctions {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    class DoSomething: BridgeFunction {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        func execute(parameters: [String: Any]) throws -> [String: Any] {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            let option = parameters["option"] as? String ?? ""
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            // Do your native work here
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            return BridgeResponse.success(data: [
plugins/bridge-functions.md:                "result": "completed",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:                "option": option
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            ])
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:}
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Key points:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- Implement the `BridgeFunction` protocol
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- Parameters come as a dictionary
plugins/bridge-functions.md:- Return using `BridgeResponse.success()` or `BridgeResponse.error()`
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Kotlin Implementation (Android)
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Create your functions in `resources/android/src/`. Use your own vendor-namespaced package:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```kotlin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:package com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:import com.nativephp.mobile.bridge.BridgeFunction
plugins/bridge-functions.md:import com.nativephp.mobile.bridge.BridgeResponse
plugins/bridge-functions.md:object MyPluginFunctions {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    class DoSomething : BridgeFunction {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        override fun execute(parameters: Map<String, Any>): Map<String, Any> {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            val option = parameters["option"] as? String ?: ""
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            // Do your native work here
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            return BridgeResponse.success(mapOf(
plugins/bridge-functions.md:                "result" to "completed",
plugins/bridge-functions.md:                "option" to option
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            ))
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:}
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:The package declaration determines where your file is placed during compilation. Using `com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin` ensures
plugins/bridge-functions.md:your code is isolated from other plugins and the core NativePHP code.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Calling from PHP
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Create a facade method that calls your bridge function:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```php
plugins/bridge-functions.md:class MyPlugin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:{
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    public function doSomething(array $options = []): mixed
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        if (function_exists('nativephp_call')) {
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            $result = nativephp_call('MyPlugin.DoSomething', json_encode($options));
plugins/bridge-functions.md:            return json_decode($result)?->data;
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:        return null;
plugins/bridge-functions.md:    }
plugins/bridge-functions.md:}
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Error Handling
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Return errors from native code using `BridgeResponse.error()`:
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```swift
plugins/bridge-functions.md:// Swift
plugins/bridge-functions.md:return BridgeResponse.error(message: "Something went wrong")
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```kotlin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:// Kotlin
plugins/bridge-functions.md:return BridgeResponse.error("Something went wrong")
plugins/bridge-functions.md:```
plugins/bridge-functions.md:The error message is available in PHP through the response.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:## Official Plugins & Dev Kit
plugins/bridge-functions.md:Need native functionality without writing Kotlin or Swift? Browse ready-made plugins or get the Dev Kit to build your own.
plugins/bridge-functions.md:[Visit the NativePHP Plugin Marketplace →](https://nativephp.com/plugins)

plugins/creating-plugins.md:---
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Scaffolding a Plugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The quickest way to create a plugin is with the interactive scaffolding command:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:create
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This walks you through naming, namespace selection, and feature options, then generates a complete plugin structure.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The first prompt asks which kind of plugin you're building. A **system plugin** adds native capabilities you call from
plugins/creating-plugins.md:PHP — the rest of this page. A **UI component plugin** adds new EDGE elements rendered by your own SwiftUI and Compose
plugins/creating-plugins.md:code; see [UI Component Plugins](./ui-components) for that path.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:<aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:#### Build Plugins 10x Faster
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Writing native Kotlin and Swift code is the hardest part of plugin development. The
plugins/creating-plugins.md:[NativePHP Plugin Development Kit](/products/plugin-dev-kit) for Claude Code can generate production-ready
plugins/creating-plugins.md:plugins in minutes — complete with bridge functions, events, permissions, and platform-specific implementations.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:[Get the Plugin Dev Kit →](/products/plugin-dev-kit)
plugins/creating-plugins.md:</aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Plugin Structure
plugins/creating-plugins.md:A plugin follows a standard layout:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:my-plugin/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:├── composer.json          # Package metadata, type must be "nativephp-plugin"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:├── nativephp.json         # Plugin manifest
plugins/creating-plugins.md:├── src/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── MyPluginServiceProvider.php
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── MyPlugin.php       # Main class
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── Facades/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   │   └── MyPlugin.php
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── Events/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   │   └── SomethingHappened.php
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   └── Commands/          # Lifecycle hook commands
plugins/creating-plugins.md:├── resources/
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── android/src/       # Kotlin bridge functions
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   ├── ios/Sources/       # Swift bridge functions
plugins/creating-plugins.md:│   └── js/                # JavaScript library stubs
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Android Package Naming
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Android/Kotlin code must declare a package at the top of each file. Use your own vendor-namespaced package to avoid
plugins/creating-plugins.md:conflicts:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```kotlin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:// resources/android/src/MyPluginFunctions.kt
plugins/creating-plugins.md:package com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:import com.nativephp.mobile.bridge.BridgeFunction
plugins/creating-plugins.md:import com.nativephp.mobile.bridge.BridgeResponse
plugins/creating-plugins.md:object MyPluginFunctions {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    class DoSomething : BridgeFunction {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        override fun execute(parameters: Map<String, Any>): Map<String, Any> {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            return BridgeResponse.success(mapOf("status" to "done"))
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The compiler places files based on their package declaration, so `package com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin` results in the file
plugins/creating-plugins.md:being placed at `app/src/main/java/com/myvendor/plugins/myplugin/MyPluginFunctions.kt`.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:<aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Files without package declarations will be placed in a fallback location, but this is not recommended. Always declare
plugins/creating-plugins.md:packages in your Kotlin files.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:</aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Reference the full package path in your manifest's bridge functions:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "bridge_functions": [{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "name": "MyPlugin.DoSomething",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "android": "com.myvendor.plugins.myplugin.MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    }]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## The composer.json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Your `composer.json` must specify the plugin type:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "name": "vendor/my-plugin",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "type": "nativephp-plugin",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "extra": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "laravel": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "providers": ["Vendor\\MyPlugin\\MyPluginServiceProvider"]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        },
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "nativephp": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "manifest": "nativephp.json"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The `type: nativephp-plugin` tells NativePHP to look for native code in this package.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## The nativephp.json Manifest
plugins/creating-plugins.md:The manifest declares native-specific configuration for your plugin. Package metadata (`name`, `version`, `description`,
plugins/creating-plugins.md:`service_provider`) comes from your `composer.json` — don't duplicate it here.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "namespace": "MyPlugin",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "bridge_functions": [
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "name": "MyPlugin.DoSomething",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "ios": "MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething",
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "android": "com.nativephp.plugins.myplugin.MyPluginFunctions.DoSomething"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    ],
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "events": ["Vendor\\MyPlugin\\Events\\SomethingHappened"],
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "android": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "permissions": ["android.permission.CAMERA"],
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "dependencies": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "implementation": ["com.google.mlkit:barcode-scanning:17.2.0"]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    },
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "ios": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "info_plist": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "NSCameraUsageDescription": "Camera is used for scanning"
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        },
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        "dependencies": {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:            "pods": [{"name": "GoogleMLKit/BarcodeScanning", "version": "~> 4.0"}]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    }
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### Manifest Fields
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| Field | Required | Description |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:|-------|----------|-------------|
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `namespace` | Yes | Namespace for the plugin (used for code generation and directory structure) |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `bridge_functions` | No | Array of native function mappings |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `events` | No | Event classes the plugin dispatches |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.permissions` | No | Android permission strings |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.features` | No | Android uses-feature declarations |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.dependencies` | No | Gradle dependencies |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.repositories` | No | Custom Maven repositories |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.activities` | No | Activities to register in manifest |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.services` | No | Services to register in manifest |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.receivers` | No | Broadcast receivers to register |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.providers` | No | Content providers to register |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.meta_data` | No | Application meta-data entries |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.min_version` | No | Minimum Android SDK version required |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `android.init_function` | No | Native function to call during app initialization |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.info_plist` | No | Info.plist entries (permissions, API keys) |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.dependencies` | No | Swift packages and CocoaPods |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.background_modes` | No | UIBackgroundModes values |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.entitlements` | No | App entitlements |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.capabilities` | No | iOS capabilities for Xcode project |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.min_version` | No | Minimum iOS version required |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `ios.init_function` | No | Native function to call during app initialization |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `assets` | No | Declarative asset copying |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `hooks` | No | Lifecycle hook commands |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:| `secrets` | No | Required environment variables |
plugins/creating-plugins.md:See [Advanced Configuration](advanced-configuration) for detailed documentation on each field.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Local Development
plugins/creating-plugins.md:During development, add your plugin to your app's `composer.json` as a path repository:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```json
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    "repositories": [
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        {"type": "path", "url": "../packages/my-plugin"}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    ]
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Then require it:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:composer require vendor/my-plugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Changes to your plugin's PHP code are picked up immediately. Changes to native code require a rebuild with
plugins/creating-plugins.md:`php artisan native:run`.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:When testing significant changes to your plugin's native code or manifest, you may need to force a fresh install of
plugins/creating-plugins.md:the native projects:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:install --force
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This ensures the native projects are rebuilt from scratch with your latest plugin configuration.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:<aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:#### Validate Early and Often
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Run `php artisan native:plugin:validate` to catch manifest errors, missing native code, or mismatched function
plugins/creating-plugins.md:declarations before you try to build.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:</aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## Registering Plugins
plugins/creating-plugins.md:After installing a plugin with Composer, you need to register it so it gets compiled into your native builds.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### First Time Setup
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Publish the NativeServiceProvider:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan vendor:publish --tag=nativephp-plugins-provider
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This creates `app/Providers/NativeServiceProvider.php`.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### Register a Plugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:register vendor/plugin-name
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This automatically adds the plugin's service provider to your `plugins()` array:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```php
plugins/creating-plugins.md:public function plugins(): array
plugins/creating-plugins.md:{
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    return [
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        \Vendor\PluginName\PluginNameServiceProvider::class,
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    ];
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### List Plugins
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:# Show registered plugins
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:list
plugins/creating-plugins.md:# Show all installed plugins (including unregistered)
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:list --all
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:### Remove a Plugin
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```shell
plugins/creating-plugins.md:php artisan native:plugin:register vendor/plugin-name --remove
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:<aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:This explicit registration is a security measure. It prevents transitive dependencies from automatically
plugins/creating-plugins.md:registering plugins without your consent.
plugins/creating-plugins.md:</aside>
plugins/creating-plugins.md:## JavaScript Library
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Plugins can provide a JavaScript library for SPA frameworks. The scaffolding creates a stub in `resources/js/`:
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```js
plugins/creating-plugins.md:// resources/js/myPlugin.js
plugins/creating-plugins.md:const baseUrl = '/_native/api/call';
plugins/creating-plugins.md:async function bridgeCall(method, params = {}) {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    const response = await fetch(baseUrl, {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        method: 'POST',
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
plugins/creating-plugins.md:        body: JSON.stringify({ method, params })
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    });
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    return response.json();
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:export async function doSomething(options = {}) {
plugins/creating-plugins.md:    return bridgeCall('MyPlugin.DoSomething', options);
plugins/creating-plugins.md:}
plugins/creating-plugins.md:```
plugins/creating-plugins.md:Users can then import your functions directly in Vue, React, or vanilla JS.
