--- title: Command Reference order: 350 --- A complete reference of all `native:*` Artisan commands available in NativePHP Mobile. ## Development Commands ### native:install Install NativePHP into your Laravel application. ```shell php artisan native:install {platform?} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `platform` | Target platform: `android`, `ios`, or `both` | | `--no-force` | Keep existing files instead of overwriting them (overwriting is the default) | | `--with-icu` | Include ICU support for Android (adds ~30MB) | | `--skip-php` | Do not download the PHP binaries | | `-F`, `--force` | Force re-download of the PHP binaries by clearing the cache | ### native:run Build and run your app on a device or simulator. ```shell php artisan native:run {os?} {udid?} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|---------------------------------------------------| | `os` | Target platform: `ios/i` or `android/a` | | `udid` | Specific device/simulator UDID | | `--build=debug` | Build type: `debug`, `release`, `bundle`, or `profileable` | | `--watch` | Enable hot reloading during development | | `--vite` | Start the Vite dev server for JS/CSS HMR (opt-in; off by default) | | `--start-url=` | Initial URL/path to load (e.g., `/dashboard`) | | `--no-tty` | Disable TTY mode for non-interactive environments |
Before building, `native:run` checks for unregistered plugins and warns you if any are found. You can register them with `php artisan native:plugin:register`.
The debug builds `native:run` produces are left on disk: the iOS simulator app at `nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/NativePHP-simulator.app` and the Android APK at `nativephp/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`. See [Finding the built app](development#finding-the-built-app). ### native:watch Watch for file changes and sync to a running mobile app. ```shell php artisan native:watch {platform?} {target?} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-----------------------------------------| | `platform` | Target platform: `ios/i` or `android/a` | | `target` | The device/simulator UDID to watch | | `--vite` | Start the Vite dev server for JS/CSS HMR (opt-in; off by default) |
The Vite dev server is **opt-in** — pass `--vite` to `native:run`/`native:watch` to start it. It was previously started automatically; the old `--no-vite` flag still exists but is now redundant. See the [Upgrade Guide](upgrade-guide).
### native:jump Start the NativePHP development server for testing mobile apps without building. ```shell php artisan native:jump ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--host=0.0.0.0` | Host address to serve on | | `--ip=` v3.3+ | IP address to display in the QR code (overrides auto-detection) | | `--http-port=` | HTTP port to serve on (defaults to `nativephp.server.http_port`, typically `3000`) | | `--ws-port=` v3.3+ | WebSocket bridge port (defaults to `3001`) | | `--bridge-port=` v3.3+ | Internal TCP bridge port (defaults to `3002`) | | `--vite-proxy-port=` v3.3+ | Port Jump uses to proxy Vite HMR to the phone (defaults to `3003`) | | `--no-serve` v3.3+ | Do not start `artisan serve` automatically (use if running your own server) | | `--laravel-port=` | Laravel dev server port (defaults to `8000`; auto-detected when `artisan serve` is managed) | | `--no-mdns` | Disable mDNS service advertisement | | `--browser` | Open the QR code page in the default browser (useful when terminal rendering is unreliable) | ### native:open Open the native project in Xcode or Android Studio. ```shell php artisan native:open {os?} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-----------------------------------------| | `os` | Target platform: `ios/i` or `android/a` | ### native:tail Tail Laravel logs from a running Android app. (Android only) ```shell php artisan native:tail ``` ### native:version Display the current NativePHP Mobile version. ```shell php artisan native:version ``` ### native:make Create a new `NativeComponent` class and its Blade view. ```shell php artisan native:make {name} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `name` | The component name (e.g. `Counter`, `Settings/Profile`) | | `--force` | Overwrite if the component already exists | ### native:rm Remove a `NativeComponent` class and its Blade view. ```shell php artisan native:rm {name?} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `name` | The component to remove (e.g. `Counter`, `Settings/Profile`). Optional — omit to choose interactively | ### native:make-test Create a Pest test for a `NativeComponent` screen. ```shell php artisan native:make-test {name} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `name` | The component to test (e.g. `Counter`, `Settings/Profile`, or a FQCN) | | `--force` | Overwrite if the test already exists | ### native:validate Validate native EDGE components for common errors. ```shell php artisan native:validate ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--component=` | Validate only a specific component | ### native:debug Show debug information about your NativePHP Mobile environment. ```shell php artisan native:debug ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--json` | Output as JSON | ### native:emulator List and launch an emulator or simulator. ```shell php artisan native:emulator {os} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `os` | Target platform: `android/a` or `ios/i` | ### native:sim Inspect or manage the app on the booted iOS simulator. (macOS only) ```shell php artisan native:sim {target?} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `target` | What to do: `data`, `app`, or `uninstall` (default: `data`) | | `--bundle-id=` | Override the app bundle identifier | ## Building & Release Commands
#### Skip the Complexity Managing certificates, provisioning profiles, and keystores locally is tedious and error-prone. [Bifrost](https://bifrost.nativephp.com) handles all of this for you — set credentials once, deploy with a single command, and collaborate with your team effortlessly.
### native:package Package your app for distribution with signing. ```shell php artisan native:package {platform} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|---------------------------------------------------| | `platform` | Target platform: `android/a` or `ios/i` | | `--ios` | Target iOS platform (shorthand for `platform=ios`) | | `--android` | Target Android platform (shorthand for `platform=android`) | | `--build-type=release` | Build type: `release` or `bundle` | | `--output=` | Output directory for signed artifacts | | `--jump-by=` | Add extra number to the suggested version, e.g. `--jump-by=10` to skip ahead | | `--no-tty` | Disable TTY mode for non-interactive environments | **Android Options:** | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--keystore=` | Path to Android keystore file | | `--keystore-password=` | Keystore password | | `--key-alias=` | Key alias for signing | | `--key-password=` | Key password | | `--fcm-key=` | FCM Server Key for push notifications | | `--google-service-key=` | Google Service Account Key file path | | `--upload-to-play-store` | Upload to Play Store after packaging | | `--play-store-track=internal` | Play Store track: `internal`, `alpha`, `beta`, `production` | | `--test-push=` | Test Play Store upload with existing AAB file (skip build) | | `--skip-prepare` | Skip prepareAndroidBuild() to preserve existing project files | **iOS Options:** | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--export-method=app-store` | Export method: `app-store`, `ad-hoc`, `enterprise`, `development` | | `--upload-to-app-store` | Upload to App Store Connect after packaging | | `--test-upload` | Test upload existing IPA (skip build) | | `--validate-only` | Only validate the archive without exporting | | `--validate-profile` | Validate provisioning profile entitlements | | `--rebuild` | Force rebuild by removing existing archive | | `--clean-caches` | Clear Xcode and SPM caches before building | | `--api-key=` | Path to App Store Connect API key file (.p8) | | `--api-key-id=` | App Store Connect API key ID | | `--api-issuer-id=` | App Store Connect API issuer ID | | `--certificate-path=` | Path to distribution certificate (.p12/.cer) | | `--certificate-password=` | Certificate password | | `--provisioning-profile-path=` | Path to provisioning profile (.mobileprovision) | | `--team-id=` | Apple Developer Team ID | ### native:release Bump the version number in your `.env` file. ```shell php artisan native:release {type} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `type` | Release type: `patch`, `minor`, or `major` | ### native:credentials Generate signing credentials for iOS and Android. ```shell php artisan native:credentials {platform?} ``` | Option | Description | |--------|--------------------------------------------------| | `platform` | Target platform: `android/a`, `ios/i`, or `both` | | `--reset` | Generate new keystore and PEM certificate | ### native:check-build-number Validate and suggest build numbers for your app. ```shell php artisan native:check-build-number ``` ## Plugin Commands ### native:plugin:create Scaffold a new NativePHP plugin interactively. ```shell php artisan native:plugin:create ``` ### native:plugin:list List all installed NativePHP plugins. ```shell php artisan native:plugin:list ``` | Option | Description | |--------|-------------| | `--json` | Output as JSON | | `--all` | Show all installed plugins, including unregistered | ### native:plugin:register             // Surface variant = filled text fields, muted tonal surfaces.
            // on-surface-variant = muted label/hint text on those surfaces.

            // Text-field container, for the OUTLINED variant. Both are unset
            // on purpose, and unset means "transparent box, Material 3
            // defaults inside" — the outlined field then reads as whatever is
            // behind it, which is correct on a plain page and invisible on a

            'success' => '#15803D',
            'on-success' => '#FFFFFF',

            'accent' => '#C2410C',
            'on-accent' => '#FFFFFF',
        ],

    /*
    |---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Fonts
    |---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Semantic names for bundled fonts (resources/fonts/ file tokens, minus
    | the extension). Use an alias anywhere a font token works — the `font`
    | attribute (`font="accent"`), chrome ->font() builders, or the layout
    | $font property. The `default` alias is the app-wide default font:
    | 'System' resolves to the platform face (San Francisco on iOS, Roboto
    | on Android); set a bundled token to apply it everywhere. Download one
    | with `php artisan native:font Inter --default`. Per-element `font`
    | attributes and font-serif / font-mono classes still win over the default.
    |
    | Weights: a family's `-Regular` token (or its bare family name, e.g.
    | 'Inter') follows the font-medium / font-semibold / font-bold classes by
    | drawing the sibling file bundled for that weight — Inter-Medium,
    | Inter-SemiBold, Inter-Bold — the names `native:font` downloads. A missing
    | weight uses the nearest bundled one; a variable font moves along its
    | weight axis instead. Any other face ('Inter-Bold') is drawn as named.

    |   'fonts' => [
    |       'default' => 'Inter-Regular',

    |   ],

    */

        'default' => 'System',
    ],

];

    |
    | Configure which orientations your app supports on different devices.
    | This will be applied during the build process to set appropriate
    | constraints in Info.plist (iOS) and AndroidManifest.xml (Android).
    |
    | For iPhone and Android, you can configure specific orientations.
    | For iPad, when enabled above, all orientations are automatically supported
    | as required by Apple's App Store guidelines.
    |
    | If all orientations are false for iPhone, the build will fail with a
    | helpful error message. If all orientations are false for Android, the
    | build will fail with a helpful error message.
    |

        'iphone' => [

---
title: Stack
order: 400
---
## Overview
An overlay container that layers its children on top of each other — like `ZStack` in SwiftUI or `Box` in Jetpack
Compose. The first child renders at the bottom; each subsequent child is placed on top.
Useful for badges, image overlays, floating labels, and layered UI effects.
```blade
<native:stack class="w-[200] h-[200] rounded-2xl">
    <native:column class="w-full h-full bg-theme-primary rounded-2xl" />
    <native:column class="w-full h-full items-center justify-center">
        <native:text class="text-xl font-bold text-theme-on-primary">Overlay Text</native:text>
    </native:column>
</native:stack>
```
## Children
Accepts any EDGE elements as children. Children are rendered in order, with later children appearing on top of earlier
ones.
Each child is **placed at its natural size and centered** in the stack's bounds. Give a child `w-full` or `h-full` to
force it to fill the stack.
## Supported Tailwind classes
Stack inherits the full class set documented at [Layout & Styling](layout#supported-tailwind-classes). The classes
that shape how a stack behaves specifically:
| Class | Effect on a stack |
|---|---|
| `w-*`, `h-*`, fractional, arbitrary `w-[N]` / `h-[N]` | Set the stack's own bounds — children center within it |
| `flex-1` | Fills remaining space in the parent flex container |
| `self-*` | This stack's alignment within its parent (`self-start`, `self-center`, `self-end`, `self-stretch`) |
| `absolute`, `relative`, `top-N`, `right-N`, `bottom-N`, `left-N` | Position the stack itself when its parent uses absolute layout |
Everything else from the shared list applies as on any element (`p-*`, `m-*`, `bg-*`, `rounded-*`, `border-*`,
`shadow-*`, `opacity-*`, `dark:*`, `ios:*` / `android:*`, `glass:*`, alpha suffix `/N`, arbitrary `prefix-[value]`).
## Examples
### Avatar with centered badge
```blade
<native:stack class="w-[56] h-[56]">
    <native:column class="w-[56] h-[56] rounded-full bg-theme-surface-variant" />
    <native:column class="w-[20] h-[20] bg-green-500 rounded-full border-2 border-white" />
</native:stack>
```
In a real app the base layer would typically be a `<native:image>` avatar (e.g.
`<native:image src="https://i.pravatar.cc/128?img=12" class="w-[56] h-[56] rounded-full" />`).
### Badge on an icon
```blade
<native:stack class="w-[40] h-[40]">
    <native:icon name="notifications" :size="32" />
    <native:column class="w-[18] h-[18] bg-red-500 rounded-full items-center justify-center">
        <native:text class="text-[10] font-bold text-white">3</native:text>
    </native:column>
</native:stack>
```
### Image with bottom-aligned overlay
```blade
<native:stack class="w-full h-[250] rounded-2xl">
    <native:image src="https://picsum.photos/seed/banner/800/500" class="w-full h-full" fit="cover" />
    <native:column class="w-full h-full justify-end p-4 bg-black/40">
        <native:text class="text-2xl font-bold text-white">Featured Article</native:text>
        <native:text class="text-base text-white">Read more about this topic</native:text>
    </native:column>
</native:stack>
```
<aside>
For corner-anchored placement (e.g. a status dot pinned to the bottom-right of an avatar), wrap your content in a
`<native:column class="relative">` parent and use `<native:column class="absolute bottom-[0] right-[0]">` for the
anchored child. See [Positioning](../the-basics/positioning).
</aside>
## Element

use Native\Mobile\Edge\Elements\Image;

<?php

namespace App\Shop;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;
use RuntimeException;

/**
 * Plain-HTTP client for the Shopify Storefront GraphQL API (mock.shop).
 *
 * Operations are taken verbatim from resources/graphql/storefront.graphql
 * (a copy of spec/storefront.graphql). Each request sends the operation plus
 * the fragments it uses, with `operationName` always set.
 */
class Storefront
{
    /** @var array<string, string>|null name => definition source */
    private static ?array $definitions = null;

    /** @var array<string, string> operation name => document */
    private static array $documents = [];

    private static ?string $endpoint = null;

    /**
     * The endpoint to talk to. iOS: SHOP_API_URL from the process environment
     * at launch (devicectl / simctl). Android: SHOP_API_URL baked into .env at
     * build time. Otherwise the default mock.shop endpoint.
     */
    public static function endpoint(): string
    {
        if (self::$endpoint !== null) {
            return self::$endpoint;
        }

        $fromProcess = getenv('SHOP_API_URL');
        if (is_string($fromProcess) && trim($fromProcess) !== '') {
            return self::$endpoint = trim($fromProcess);
        }

        $fromConfig = config('shop.endpoint');
        if (is_string($fromConfig) && trim($fromConfig) !== '') {
            return self::$endpoint = trim($fromConfig);
        }

        return self::$endpoint = config('shop.default_endpoint');
    }

    /**
     * The GraphQL document for one operation: the fragments it spreads
     * (transitively), followed by the operation itself, all as written.
     */
    public static function document(string $operation): string
    {
        if (isset(self::$documents[$operation])) {
            return self::$documents[$operation];
        }

        $defs = self::definitions();
        if (! isset($defs[$operation])) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Unknown operation {$operation}");
        }

        $needed = [];
        $queue = [$defs[$operation]];
        while ($queue) {
            $source = array_shift($queue);
            preg_match_all('/\.\.\.\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)/', $source, $m);
            foreach ($m[1] as $name) {
                if ($name === 'on' || isset($needed[$name]) || ! isset($defs[$name])) {
                    continue;
                }
                $needed[$name] = true;
                $queue[] = $defs[$name];
            }
        }

        $parts = [];
        foreach ($defs as $name => $source) {
            if (isset($needed[$name])) {
                $parts[] = $source;
            }
        }
        $parts[] = $defs[$operation];

        return self::$documents[$operation] = implode("\n\n", $parts);
    }

    /**
     * Run one operation. Executed inside an AsyncTask (background PHP
     * thread), so everything it needs is passed in.
     *
     * @return array<string, mixed> the `data` object
     */
    public static function send(string $endpoint, string $operation, string $document, array $variables): array
    {
        $response = Http::connectTimeout(8)
            ->timeout(20)
            ->acceptJson()
            ->withBody(json_encode([
                'operationName' => $operation,
                'query' => $document,
                'variables' => (object) $variables,
            ], JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES), 'application/json')
            ->post($endpoint);

        if (! $response->successful()) {
            throw new RuntimeException("{$operation} failed with HTTP {$response->status()}");
        }

        $json = $response->json();
        if (! is_array($json) || ! isset($json['data']) || ! is_array($json['data'])) {
            $message = $json['errors'][0]['message'] ?? 'Malformed response';
            throw new RuntimeException("{$operation} failed: {$message}");
        }

        return $json['data'];
    }

    /** @return array<string, string> */
    private static function definitions(): array
    {
        if (self::$definitions !== null) {
            return self::$definitions;
        }

        $source = file_get_contents(resource_path('graphql/storefront.graphql'));
        $defs = [];
        $length = strlen($source);
        $i = 0;
        while ($i < $length) {
            if (! preg_match('/(fragment|query|mutation)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)/A', $source, $m, 0, $i)) {
                $i++;

                continue;
            }
            $start = $i;
            $open = strpos($source, '{', $i);
            $depth = 0;
            for ($j = $open; $j < $length; $j++) {
                if ($source[$j] === '{') {
                    $depth++;
                } elseif ($source[$j] === '}') {
                    $depth--;
                    if ($depth === 0) {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            $defs[$m[2]] = substr($source, $start, $j - $start + 1);
            $i = $j + 1;
        }

        return self::$definitions = $defs;
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Shop;

/**
 * Turns Storefront API payloads into the flat arrays the views render.
 */
class Format
{
    /** `{amount: "75.0"}` → `$75.00`. All prices are USD. */
    public static function money(?array $money): string
    {
        return '$'.number_format((float) ($money['amount'] ?? 0), 2, '.', '');
    }

    /** Append the `width` query parameter to an API image URL. */
    public static function image(?string $url, int $width): ?string
    {
        if ($url === null || $url === '') {
            return null;
        }

        return $url.(str_contains($url, '?') ? '&' : '?').'width='.$width;
    }

    /**
     * A ProductCard fragment → card data.
     *
     * @return array{handle: string, title: string, image: ?string, thumb: ?string, price: string, compare: ?string}
     */
    public static function card(array $node): array
    {
        $price = $node['priceRange']['minVariantPrice'] ?? null;
        $compare = $node['compareAtPriceRange']['minVariantPrice'] ?? null;
        $onSale = $compare !== null && (float) $compare['amount'] > (float) ($price['amount'] ?? 0);
        $image = $node['featuredImage']['url'] ?? null;

        return [
            'handle' => (string) ($node['handle'] ?? ''),
            'title' => (string) ($node['title'] ?? ''),
            'image' => self::image($image, 480),
            'thumb' => self::image($image, 240),
            'price' => self::money($price),
            'compare' => $onSale ? self::money($compare) : null,
        ];
    }

---
title: Button
order: 140
---
## Overview
A native button. Renders as a SwiftUI `Button` with `buttonStyle(...)` on iOS and a Material3 `Button` on Android.
Visual styling follows Model 3 — colors, radius, shadow, and typography come from the theme. There are intentionally
**no per-instance** color, background, border, radius, shadow, font-size, or font-weight overrides. For full visual
control drop to a [`<native:pressable>`](pressable) wrapping your own content.
```blade
<native:button label="Get Started" @press="handleStart" />
```
`@press` names a public method on your component — tapping this button calls `handleStart()`.
## Props
The label can be passed as the `label` attribute or as slot content between the tags. If both are set, `label` wins.
Slot content is treated as plain text — nested tags are stripped and whitespace is collapsed. Use the `icon` /
`icon-trailing` props to add icons rather than nesting elements in the slot.
- `label` - Button text (optional if using slot content)
- `variant` - Semantic style: `primary` (default), `secondary`, `destructive`, `ghost`. Each fills its theme
  token solid; for a softer tonal fill, set opacity on the token itself (e.g. `'secondary' => 'fuchsia-500/70'`
  in `config/native-ui.php`) — see [Theming](../digging-deeper/theming)
- `size` - `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`
- `icon` - A leading [icon](icon#icon-name-reference) name (optional)
- `ios-icon` / `android-icon` <x-docs.version-badge package="mobile-ui" since="0.4" /> - Per-platform overrides for the leading icon: an [SF Symbol](icon#ios-sf-symbols)
  name on iOS, a [Material Icon](icon#android-material-icons) name on Android. `icon` is the fallback on whichever
  platform has no override — or skip it and declare only per-platform icons. `iosIcon` / `androidIcon` and the
  `<native:icon>`-style `ios` / `android` are accepted as aliases
- `icon-trailing` - A trailing [icon](icon#icon-name-reference) name (optional)
- `ios-icon-trailing` / `android-icon-trailing` <x-docs.version-badge package="mobile-ui" since="0.4" /> - Per-platform overrides for the trailing icon, mirroring
  `ios-icon` / `android-icon` (camelCase aliases accepted; no `ios` / `android` shorthand for this slot)
- `font` - Custom font for the label: a `resources/fonts/` file token or a config alias like `accent` (optional, string) — see [Text › Custom fonts](text#custom-fonts)
- `line-height` - Label line height as a multiplier of the font size (optional, float)
- `line-height-px` - Label line height as an absolute value in pixels (optional, float)
- `disabled` - Disable the button (optional, boolean, default: `false`). Disabled buttons render with the theme's
  `surface-variant` fill and `on-surface-variant` label on both platforms
- `loading` - Show a spinner in place of the leading icon and prevent presses (optional, boolean, default: `false`).
  Styled like `disabled` while the spinner runs
- `a11y-label` - Accessibility label override (optional)
- `a11y-hint` - Accessibility hint (optional)
- `menu` - Attach a tap-to-open dropdown menu — an array of [`NavAction`](menus) items. Tapping opens the menu
  instead of firing `@press`. See [Menus](menus)
## Events
- `@press` - Component method to call when tapped
<aside>
Layout attributes (`width`, `height`, `flex-grow`, `margin`, `align-self`) flow through to position the button
inside its parent. Per-instance `padding`, `bg`, `border-*`, `border-radius`, `elevation`, `opacity`, `font-*`
attributes are intentionally dropped before reaching the renderer.
</aside>
## Examples
### Variants
```blade
<native:column class="w-full gap-3 p-4">
    <native:button label="Save"   variant="primary"     @press="save" />
    <native:button label="Cancel" variant="secondary"   @press="cancel" />
    <native:button label="Delete" variant="destructive" @press="delete" />
    <native:button label="Skip"   variant="ghost"       @press="skip" />
</native:column>
```
### Sizes
```blade
<native:row class="gap-2 items-center">
    <native:button label="Small"  size="sm" @press="action" />
    <native:button label="Medium" size="md" @press="action" />
    <native:button label="Large"  size="lg" @press="action" />
</native:row>
```
### With icons
```blade
<native:button
    label="Continue"
    icon="check"
    icon-trailing="forward"
    @press="next"
/>
```
### Platform icons
<x-docs.version-badge package="mobile-ui" since="0.4" />
When one shared name doesn't map well on both platforms, give each platform its own symbol — an
[SF Symbol](icon#ios-sf-symbols) name on iOS, a [Material Icon](icon#android-material-icons) name on Android:
```blade
<native:button
    label="Tap to Pay"
    ios-icon="wave.3.right"
    android-icon="nfc"
    @press="startPayment"
/>
```
Resolution happens per platform: each side uses its override, falling back to `icon` where none is given. Bound
`:ios-icon` / `:android-icon` also accept `App\Icons` enum cases, exactly like
[`<native:icon>`'s `:ios` / `:android`](icon#typed-icon-enums). The trailing slot works the same way via

<?php

namespace App\NativeComponents;

use App\Shop\Format;
use App\Shop\Storefront;
use Illuminate\View\View;
use Native\Mobile\AsyncTask;
use Native\Mobile\Edge\NativeComponent;
use Native\Mobile\Facades\Browser;
use Native\Mobile\Facades\Dialog;
use Shopbench\Native\PlatformLog;
use Throwable;

/**
 * The whole Everbloom app is one native screen.
 *
 * NativePHP's router keeps a single navigation stack, and its native tab bar
 * rebuilds a tab's screens when you switch back to it. The spec wants three
 * tabs that each keep their own stack, so this screen holds the three stacks
 * itself and renders the screen on top of the active one, plus a tab bar
 * drawn with EDGE elements (which also carries the accessibility identifiers
 * the benchmark needs).
 *
 * Each pushed screen is a plain state array in $screens, keyed by id. Network
 * requests run on NativePHP's background PHP lane (AsyncTask); responses are
 * applied only if the screen still exists and the request is still the
 * latest one for it.
 */
class Shell extends NativeComponent
{
    private const PAGE_SIZE = 24;

    private const SORTS = [
        'featured' => ['COLLECTION_DEFAULT', false],
        'best-selling' => ['BEST_SELLING', false],
        'price-asc' => ['PRICE', false],
        'price-desc' => ['PRICE', true],
    ];

    /** Active tab: home | search | cart. */
    public string $tab = 'home';

    /** @var array<string, list<string>> tab => screen ids, bottom to top */
    public array $stacks = [
        'home' => ['home'],
        'search' => ['search'],
        'cart' => ['cart'],
    ];

    /** @var array<string, array> screen id => screen state */
    public array $screens = [];

    public int $seq = 0;

    /** The in-memory cart (Format::cart()), null before the first add. */
    public ?array $cart = null;

    public bool $cartBusy = false;

    /** Bound to the search field (debounced 300 ms natively). */
    public string $searchQuery = '';

    private static bool $homeReadyLogged = false;

    public function mount(): void
    {
        $this->screens = [
            'home' => ['type' => 'home', 'status' => 'loading', 'req' => 0, 'collections' => [], 'products' => []],
            'search' => [
                'type' => 'search', 'status' => 'idle', 'req' => 0, 'query' => '',
                'results' => [], 'total' => 0, 'cursor' => null, 'hasNext' => false, 'loadingMore' => false,
            ],
            'cart' => ['type' => 'cart'],
        ];

        $this->loadHome();
    }

    // ── Navigation ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function selectTab(string $tab): void
    {
        if (isset($this->stacks[$tab])) {
            $this->tab = $tab;
        }
    }

    public function goBack(): void
    {
        if (count($this->stacks[$this->tab]) <= 1) {
            return;
        }

        $id = array_pop($this->stacks[$this->tab]);
        unset($this->screens[$id]);
    }

    public function onBackPressed(): void
    {
        if (count($this->stacks[$this->tab]) > 1) {
            $this->goBack();

            return;
        }

        $this->back();
    }

    private function push(array $screen): string
    {
        $id = 'p'.(++$this->seq);
        $this->screens[$id] = $screen;
        $this->stacks[$this->tab][] = $id;

        return $id;
    }

    // ── Home ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function loadHome(): void
    {
        $this->screens['home']['status'] = 'loading';
        $req = ++$this->screens['home']['req'];

        $this->request('Home', [], function (array $data) use ($req) {
            if (($this->screens['home']['req'] ?? null) !== $req) {
                return;
            }

            $collections = [];
            foreach ($data['collections']['nodes'] ?? [] as $node) {
                $url = $node['image']['url'] ?? null;
                $collections[] = [
                    'handle' => (string) $node['handle'],
                    'title' => (string) $node['title'],
                    'image' => Format::image($url, 480),
                    'banner' => Format::image($url, 1080),
                ];
            }

            $this->screens['home']['collections'] = $collections;
            $this->screens['home']['products'] = Format::cards($data['products']['nodes'] ?? []);
            $this->screens['home']['status'] = 'loaded';
        }, function () use ($req) {
            if (($this->screens['home']['req'] ?? null) === $req) {
                $this->screens['home']['status'] = 'error';
            }
        });
    }

    // ── Collection ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function openCollection(string $handle): void
    {
        $title = '';
        foreach ($this->screens['home']['collections'] as $collection) {
            if ($collection['handle'] === $handle) {
                $title = $collection['title'];
                break;
            }
        }

        $id = $this->push([
            'type' => 'collection', 'handle' => $handle, 'title' => $title, 'description' => '',
            'sort' => 'featured', 'status' => 'loading', 'req' => 0,
            'products' => [], 'cursor' => null, 'hasNext' => false, 'loadingMore' => false,
        ]);

        $this->loadCollection($id);
    }

    public function setSort(string $id, string $sort): void
    {
        if (! isset($this->screens[$id], self::SORTS[$sort]) || $this->screens[$id]['sort'] === $sort) {
            return;
        }

        $this->screens[$id]['sort'] = $sort;
        $this->loadCollection($id);
    }

    public function retryCollection(string $id): void
    {
        if (isset($this->screens[$id])) {
            $this->loadCollection($id);
        }
    }

    public function loadMoreProducts(string $id): void
    {
        $screen = $this->screens[$id] ?? null;
        if ($screen === null || $screen['status'] !== 'loaded' || ! $screen['hasNext'] || $screen['loadingMore']) {
            return;
        }

        $this->loadCollection($id, more: true);
    }

    private function loadCollection(string $id, bool $more = false): void
    {
        $screen = &$this->screens[$id];

        if ($more) {
            $screen['loadingMore'] = true;
        } else {
            $screen['status'] = 'loading';
            $screen['products'] = [];
            $screen['cursor'] = null;
            $screen['hasNext'] = false;
            $screen['loadingMore'] = false;
        }

        $req = ++$screen['req'];
        [$sortKey, $reverse] = self::SORTS[$screen['sort']];
        $variables = [
            'handle' => $screen['handle'],
            'first' => self::PAGE_SIZE,
            'sortKey' => $sortKey,
            'reverse' => $reverse,
        ];
        if ($more) {
            $variables['after'] = $screen['cursor'];
        }
        unset($screen);

        $this->request('CollectionProducts', $variables, function (array $data) use ($id, $req, $more) {
            if (($this->screens[$id]['req'] ?? null) !== $req) {
                return;
            }

            $collection = $data['collection'] ?? null;
            if (! is_array($collection)) {
                $this->screens[$id]['loadingMore'] = false;
                if (! $more) {
                    $this->screens[$id]['status'] = 'error';
                }

                return;
            }

            $page = $collection['products'] ?? [];
            $screen = &$this->screens[$id];
            $screen['title'] = (string) ($collection['title'] ?? $screen['title']);
            $screen['description'] = (string) ($collection['description'] ?? '');
            $screen['products'] = array_merge($screen['products'], Format::cards($page['nodes'] ?? []));
            $screen['cursor'] = $page['pageInfo']['endCursor'] ?? null;
            $screen['hasNext'] = (bool) ($page['pageInfo']['hasNextPage'] ?? false);
            $screen['loadingMore'] = false;
            $screen['status'] = 'loaded';
        }, function () use ($id, $req, $more) {
            if (($this->screens[$id]['req'] ?? null) !== $req) {
                return;
            }

            $this->screens[$id]['loadingMore'] = false;
            if (! $more) {
                $this->screens[$id]['status'] = 'error';
            }
        });
    }

    // ── Product ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function openProduct(string $handle): void
    {
        $id = $this->push([
            'type' => 'product', 'handle' => $handle, 'status' => 'loading', 'req' => 0,
            'product' => null, 'recs' => [], 'variant' => null, 'image' => 0, 'adding' => false,
        ]);

        $this->loadProduct($id);
    }

    public function retryProduct(string $id): void
    {
        if (isset($this->screens[$id])) {
            $this->loadProduct($id);
        }
    }

    private function loadProduct(string $id): void
    {
        $this->screens[$id]['status'] = 'loading';
        $req = ++$this->screens[$id]['req'];

        $this->request('Product', ['handle' => $this->screens[$id]['handle']], function (array $data) use ($id, $req) {
            if (($this->screens[$id]['req'] ?? null) !== $req) {
                return;
            }

            $product = $data['product'] ?? null;
            if (! is_array($product)) {
                $this->screens[$id]['status'] = 'error';

                return;
            }

            $variants = [];
            foreach ($product['variants']['nodes'] ?? [] as $node) {
                $options = [];
                foreach ($node['selectedOptions'] ?? [] as $option) {
                    $options[$option['name']] = $option['value'];
                }
                $onSale = isset($node['compareAtPrice']['amount'])
                    && (float) $node['compareAtPrice']['amount'] > (float) ($node['price']['amount'] ?? 0);
                $variants[] = [
                    'id' => (string) $node['id'],
                    'available' => (bool) ($node['availableForSale'] ?? false),
                    'options' => $options,
                    'price' => Format::money($node['price'] ?? null),
                    'compare' => $onSale ? Format::money($node['compareAtPrice']) : null,
                ];
            }

            $options = [];
            foreach ($product['options'] ?? [] as $option) {
                $values = array_map(fn ($v) => (string) $v['name'], $option['optionValues'] ?? []);
                if ($option['name'] === 'Title' && $values === ['Default Title']) {
                    continue;
                }
                $options[] = ['name' => (string) $option['name'], 'values' => $values];
            }

            $selected = null;
            foreach ($variants as $index => $variant) {
                if ($variant['available']) {
                    $selected = $index;
                    break;
                }
            }

            $images = [];
            foreach (array_slice($product['images']['nodes'] ?? [], 0, 10) as $image) {
                $images[] = Format::image($image['url'] ?? null, 1080);
            }

            $screen = &$this->screens[$id];
            $screen['product'] = [
                'title' => (string) $product['title'],
                'description' => (string) ($product['description'] ?? ''),
                'images' => $images,
                'options' => $options,
                'variants' => $variants,
            ];
            $screen['variant'] = $variants === [] ? null : ($selected ?? 0);
            $screen['recs'] = Format::cards($data['productRecommendations'] ?? []);
            $screen['image'] = 0;
            $screen['status'] = 'loaded';
        }, function () use ($id, $req) {
            if (($this->screens[$id]['req'] ?? null) === $req) {
                $this->screens[$id]['status'] = 'error';
            }
        });
    }

    public function showImage(string $id, int $index): void
    {
        if (isset($this->screens[$id])) {
            $this->screens[$id]['image'] = $index;
        }
    }

    public function selectOption(string $id, int $optionIndex, int $valueIndex): void
    {
        $product = $this->screens[$id]['product'] ?? null;
        $option = $product['options'][$optionIndex] ?? null;
        $value = $option['values'][$valueIndex] ?? null;
        if ($option === null || $value === null) {
            return;
        }

        $current = $product['variants'][$this->screens[$id]['variant']]['options'] ?? [];
        $wanted = array_merge($current, [$option['name'] => $value]);

        $match = null;
        foreach ($product['variants'] as $index => $variant) {
            if ($variant['options'] == $wanted) {
                $match = $index;
                break;
            }
        }
        if ($match === null) {
            foreach ($product['variants'] as $index => $variant) {
                if (($variant['options'][$option['name']] ?? null) === $value) {
                    $match = $index;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        if ($match !== null) {
            $this->screens[$id]['variant'] = $match;
        }
    }

    public function addToCart(string $id): void
    {
        $screen = $this->screens[$id] ?? null;
        $variant = $screen['product']['variants'][$screen['variant'] ?? -1] ?? null;
        if ($variant === null || $screen['adding'] || $this->cartBusy) {
            return;
        }

        $this->screens[$id]['adding'] = true;
        $this->cartBusy = true;
        $lines = [['merchandiseId' => $variant['id'], 'quantity' => 1]];

        [$operation, $variables, $key] = $this->cart === null
            ? ['CartCreate', ['lines' => $lines], 'cartCreate']
            : ['CartLinesAdd', ['cartId' => $this->cart['id'], 'lines' => $lines], 'cartLinesAdd'];

        $this->request($operation, $variables, function (array $data) use ($id, $key) {
            $this->cartBusy = false;
            if (isset($this->screens[$id])) {
                $this->screens[$id]['adding'] = false;
            }
            if ($this->applyCartPayload($data[$key] ?? null)) {
                $this->tab = 'cart';
            }
        }, function () use ($id) {
            $this->cartBusy = false;
            if (isset($this->screens[$id])) {
                $this->screens[$id]['adding'] = false;
            }
            Dialog::alert('Couldn’t add to cart', 'Check your connection and try again.', ['OK']);
        });
    }

    // ── Cart ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function changeQuantity(int $index, int $delta): void
    {
        $line = $this->cart['lines'][$index] ?? null;
        if ($line === null || $this->cartBusy) {
            return;
        }

        $this->cartBusy = true;
        $variables = [
            'cartId' => $this->cart['id'],
            'lines' => [['id' => $line['id'], 'quantity' => max(0, $line['quantity'] + $delta)]],
        ];

        $this->request('CartLinesUpdate', $variables, function (array $data) {
            $this->cartBusy = false;
            $this->applyCartPayload($data['cartLinesUpdate'] ?? null);
        }, function () {
            $this->cartBusy = false;
            Dialog::alert('Couldn’t update cart', 'Check your connection and try again.', ['OK']);
        });
    }

    public function checkout(): void
    {
        if (! empty($this->cart['checkoutUrl'])) {
            Browser::inApp($this->cart['checkoutUrl']);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Replace the cart with the one in a cart mutation payload and surface the
     * first user error. Returns true when the payload carried no user errors.
     */
    private function applyCartPayload(?array $payload): bool
    {
        if ($payload === null) {
            return false;
        }

        if (isset($payload['cart']) && is_array($payload['cart'])) {
            $this->cart = Format::cart($payload['cart']);
        }

        $errors = $payload['userErrors'] ?? [];
        if ($errors !== []) {
            Dialog::alert('Cart', (string) ($errors[0]['message'] ?? 'Something went wrong.'), ['OK']);

            return false;
        }

        return true;
    }

    // ── Search ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function updatedSearchQuery(): void
    {
        if (trim($this->searchQuery) !== $this->screens['search']['query'] || $this->screens['search']['status'] === 'error') {
            $this->search();
        }
    }

    public function retrySearch(): void
    {
        $this->search();
    }

    public function loadMoreResults(): void
    {
        $screen = $this->screens['search'];
        if ($screen['status'] !== 'loaded' || ! $screen['hasNext'] || $screen['loadingMore']) {
            return;
        }

        $this->search(more: true);
    }

    private function search(bool $more = false): void
    {
        $screen = &$this->screens['search'];
        $req = ++$screen['req'];

        if ($more) {
            $query = $screen['query'];
            $screen['loadingMore'] = true;
        } else {
            $query = trim($this->searchQuery);
            $screen['query'] = $query;
            $screen['results'] = [];
            $screen['total'] = 0;
            $screen['cursor'] = null;
            $screen['hasNext'] = false;
            $screen['loadingMore'] = false;
            $screen['status'] = $query === '' ? 'idle' : 'loading';
        }

        $variables = ['query' => $query, 'first' => self::PAGE_SIZE];
        if ($more) {
            $variables['after'] = $screen['cursor'];
        }
        unset($screen);

        if ($query === '') {
            return;
        }

        $current = fn () => ($this->screens['search']['req'] ?? null) === $req
            && $this->screens['search']['query'] === $query;

        $this->request('Search', $variables, function (array $data) use ($current) {
            if (! $current()) {
                return; // a response for a query that is no longer the current one
            }

            $search = $data['search'] ?? [];
            $screen = &$this->screens['search'];
            $screen['results'] = array_merge($screen['results'], Format::cards($search['nodes'] ?? []));
            $screen['total'] = (int) ($search['totalCount'] ?? 0);
            $screen['cursor'] = $search['pageInfo']['endCursor'] ?? null;
            $screen['hasNext'] = (bool) ($search['pageInfo']['hasNextPage'] ?? false);
            $screen['loadingMore'] = false;
            $screen['status'] = 'loaded';
        }, function () use ($current, $more) {
            if (! $current()) {
                return;
            }

            $this->screens['search']['loadingMore'] = false;
            if (! $more) {
                $this->screens['search']['status'] = 'error';
            }
        });
    }

    // ── Networking ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    /**
     * Send a Storefront operation on the background PHP lane and hand the
     * `data` object (or the failure) back to this screen.
     *
     * NativePHP refuses async tasks until its background lane is up (Android:
     * ~2.5 s after launch). A refused request runs inline instead, so the
     * first Home load never fails just because it was early.
     */
    private function request(string $operation, array $variables, \Closure $done, \Closure $fail): void
    {
        $endpoint = Storefront::endpoint();
        $document = Storefront::document($operation);
        $work = static fn () => Storefront::send($endpoint, $operation, $document, $variables);

        AsyncTask::dispatch($work)
            ->timeout(45)
            ->finished(function ($data) use ($done) {
                $done(is_array($data) ? $data : []);
            })
            ->failed(function (Throwable $e) use ($work, $done, $fail) {
                if (str_contains($e->getMessage(), 'background lane is not available')) {
                    try {
                        $data = $work();
                    } catch (Throwable $inline) {
                        $fail($inline);

                        return;
                    }
                    $done($data);

                    return;
                }

                $fail($e);
            });
    }

    // ── Render ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function render(): View
    {
        $stack = $this->stacks[$this->tab];
        $id = $stack[count($stack) - 1];
        $screen = $this->screens[$id];

        if (! self::$homeReadyLogged && $this->screens['home']['status'] === 'loaded' && $id === 'home') {
            self::$homeReadyLogged = true;
            PlatformLog::write('SHOPBENCH home_ready');
        }

        return view('native.shell', [
            'id' => $id,
            'screen' => $screen,
            'canGoBack' => count($stack) > 1,
            'cartCount' => $this->cart['totalQuantity'] ?? 0,
        ]);
    }
}

{

        'featured' => ['COLLECTION_DEFAULT', false],
        'best-selling' => ['BEST_SELLING', false],
        'price-asc' => ['PRICE', false],

    ];

    /** Active tab: home | search | cart. */
    public string $tab = 'home';

    public array $stacks = [
        'home' => ['home'],
        'search' => ['search'],
        'cart' => ['cart'],
    ];

    /** @var array<string, array> screen id => screen state */
    public array $screens = [];

    public int $seq = 0;

    public function mount(): void

                'results' => [], 'total' => 0, 'cursor' => null, 'hasNext' => false, 'loadingMore' => false,

        }
    }

    public function goBack(): void
    {
        if (count($this->stacks[$this->tab]) <= 1) {

<?php

use Native\Mobile\Facades\Browser;
use Native\Mobile\Facades\Dialog;
use Shopbench\Native\PlatformLog;
use Throwable;

/**
 * The whole Everbloom app is one native screen.
 *
 * NativePHP's router keeps a single navigation stack, and its native tab bar
 * rebuilds a tab's screens when you switch back to it. The spec wants three
 * tabs that each keep their own stack, so this screen holds the three stacks
 * itself and renders the screen on top of the active one, plus a tab bar
 * drawn with EDGE elements (which also carries the accessibility identifiers
 * the benchmark needs).
 *
 * Each pushed screen is a plain state array in $screens, keyed by id. Network
 * requests run on NativePHP's background PHP lane (AsyncTask); responses are
 * applied only if the screen still exists and the request is still the
 * latest one for it.
 */
class Shell extends NativeComponent
{
    private const PAGE_SIZE = 24;

    private const SORTS = [
        'featured' => ['COLLECTION_DEFAULT', false],
        'best-selling' => ['BEST_SELLING', false],
        'price-asc' => ['PRICE', false],
        'price-desc' => ['PRICE', true],
    ];

    /** Active tab: home | search | cart. */
    public string $tab = 'home';

    /** @var array<string, list<string>> tab => screen ids, bottom to top */
    public array $stacks = [
        'home' => ['home'],
        'search' => ['search'],
        'cart' => ['cart'],
    ];

    /** @var array<string, array> screen id => screen state */
    public array $screens = [];

    public int $seq = 0;

    /** The in-memory cart (Format::cart()), null before the first add. */

    public bool $cartBusy = false;

    public function mount(): void
    {

            'home' => ['type' => 'home', 'status' => 'loading', 'req' => 0, 'collections' => [], 'products' => []],
            'search' => [
                'type' => 'search', 'status' => 'idle', 'req' => 0, 'query' => '',
                'results' => [], 'total' => 0, 'cursor' => null, 'hasNext' => false, 'loadingMore' => false,
            ],
            'cart' => ['type' => 'cart'],
        ];

        $this->loadHome();
    }

    // ── Navigation ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function selectTab(string $tab): void
    {
        if (isset($this->stacks[$tab])) {
            $this->tab = $tab;
        }
    }

    public function goBack(): void
    {
        if (count($this->stacks[$this->tab]) <= 1) {
            return;
        }

        $id = array_pop($this->stacks[$this->tab]);
        unset($this->screens[$id]);
    }

    public function onBackPressed(): void
    {
        if (count($this->stacks[$this->tab]) > 1) {

        $this->back();

    private function push(array $screen): string

    public function loadHome(): void
    {

            if (! is_array($product)) {

            $screen['cursor'] = $search['pageInfo']['endCursor'] ?? null;
            $screen['hasNext'] = (bool) ($search['pageInfo']['hasNextPage'] ?? false);
            $screen['loadingMore'] = false;
            $screen['status'] = 'loaded';
        }, function () use ($current, $more) {
            if (! $current()) {
                return;
            }

            $this->screens['search']['loadingMore'] = false;
            if (! $more) {
                $this->screens['search']['status'] = 'error';
            }
        });
    }

    // ── Networking ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    /**
     * Send a Storefront operation on the background PHP lane and hand the
     * `data` object (or the failure) back to this screen.
     *
     * NativePHP refuses async tasks until its background lane is up (Android:
     * ~2.5 s after launch). A refused request runs inline instead, so the
     * first Home load never fails just because it was early.
     */
    private function request(string $operation, array $variables, \Closure $done, \Closure $fail): void
    {
        $endpoint = Storefront::endpoint();
        $document = Storefront::document($operation);
        $work = static fn () => Storefront::send($endpoint, $operation, $document, $variables);

        AsyncTask::dispatch($work)
            ->timeout(45)
            ->finished(function ($data) use ($done) {
                $done(is_array($data) ? $data : []);
            })
            ->failed(function (Throwable $e) use ($work, $done, $fail) {
                if (str_contains($e->getMessage(), 'background lane is not available')) {
                    try {
                        $data = $work();
                    } catch (Throwable $inline) {
                        $fail($inline);

                        return;
                    }
                    $done($data);

                    return;
                }

                $fail($e);
            });
    }

    // ── Render ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    public function render(): View
    {
        $stack = $this->stacks[$this->tab];
        $id = $stack[count($stack) - 1];
        $screen = $this->screens[$id];

        if (! self::$homeReadyLogged && $this->screens['home']['status'] === 'loaded' && $id === 'home') {
            self::$homeReadyLogged = true;
            PlatformLog::write('SHOPBENCH home_ready');
        }

        return view('native.shell', [
            'id' => $id,
            'screen' => $screen,
            'canGoBack' => count($stack) > 1,
            'cartCount' => $this->cart['totalQuantity'] ?? 0,
        ]);
    }
}

mkdir -p /Users/itome/shopbench-runs/nativephp/scripts && cat > /Users/itome/shopbench-runs/nativephp/scripts/build-ios.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the Everbloom iOS app.
#
#   scripts/build-ios.sh simulator   # iOS Simulator .app (arm64)
#   scripts/build-ios.sh device      # iOS device release .app (arm64)
#
# Device builds are signed automatically with the team in $DEVELOPMENT_TEAM;
# with it unset, code signing is disabled (CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

MODE="${1:-device}"

# Every build gets a unique build number. A NativePHP app re-extracts its
# bundled Laravel code only when the version or build number changes, so an
# install over an older build would otherwise keep running the old code.
export NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION_CODE="${NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION_CODE:-$(date +%s)}"

# 1. NativePHP: configure the Xcode project (bundle id, display name,
#    Info.plist, plugins, icons, CocoaPods/SPM), bundle the Laravel app in
#    release mode (composer --no-dev, optimized autoloader) and build the
#    simulator app.
php artisan native:build --release --simulated --no-tty

SIM_APP="$PWD/nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/NativePHP-simulator.app"
if [ "$MODE" = "simulator" ]; then
    /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :CFBundleName Everbloom" "$SIM_APP/Info.plist" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    echo "Simulator app: $SIM_APP"
    exit 0
fi

# 2. Xcode: Release configuration for generic arm64 iOS devices, reusing the
#    bundle staged in step 1 (NATIVEPHP_CLI_BUILD skips NativePHP's own
#    re-bundling build phase).
if [ -n "${DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ]; then
    SIGNING=(CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic "DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" -allowProvisioningUpdates)
else
    SIGNING=(CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO "CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=")
fi

cd nativephp/ios
NATIVEPHP_CLI_BUILD=1 xcodebuild \
    -workspace NativePHP.xcworkspace \
    -scheme NativePHP \
    -configuration Release \
    -sdk iphoneos \
    -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
    -derivedDataPath build \
    -skipPackagePluginValidation \
    "${SIGNING[@]}" \
    build

echo "Device app: $PWD/build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/NativePHP.app"
EOF
chmod +x /Users/itome/shopbench-runs/nativephp/scripts/build-ios.sh; echo ok

cat > /Users/itome/shopbench-runs/nativephp/scripts/build-android.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the Everbloom Android release APK, signed with the Android debug key.
#
#   SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api scripts/build-android.sh
#
# SHOP_API_URL (optional) is baked into the bundled app's .env at build time;
# without it the app uses https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

: "${ANDROID_HOME:=$HOME/Library/Android/sdk}"
export ANDROID_HOME
export NATIVEPHP_ANDROID_SDK_LOCATION="${NATIVEPHP_ANDROID_SDK_LOCATION:-$ANDROID_HOME}"

# Unique build number: the app re-extracts its bundled code only when the
# version or build number changes (see scripts/build-ios.sh).
export NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION_CODE="${NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION_CODE:-$(date +%s)}"

# Bake the endpoint into .env for this build (restored afterwards).
cp .env .env.build-backup
trap 'mv .env.build-backup .env' EXIT
if [ -n "${SHOP_API_URL:-}" ]; then
    if grep -q '^SHOP_API_URL=' .env; then
        sed -i.tmp "s#^SHOP_API_URL=.*#SHOP_API_URL=${SHOP_API_URL}#" .env && rm -f .env.tmp
    else
        echo "SHOP_API_URL=${SHOP_API_URL}" >> .env
    fi
fi

# NativePHP prepares the Android project (bundle, plugins, manifest) and runs
# `gradlew assembleRelease`; the release APK it produces is unsigned.
php artisan native:package android --build-type=release --no-tty --skip-prepare 2>/dev/null \
    || true
EOF

# without it the app uses https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

: "${ANDROID_HOME:=$HOME/Library/Android/sdk}"
export ANDROID_HOME
DEBUG_KEYSTORE="${DEBUG_KEYSTORE:-$HOME/.android/debug.keystore}"

# Create the standard Android debug keystore if this machine has none.
if [ ! -f "$DEBUG_KEYSTORE" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DEBUG_KEYSTORE")"
    keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore "$DEBUG_KEYSTORE" -storepass android -keypass android \
        -alias androiddebugkey -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 \
        -dname "CN=Android Debug,O=Android,C=US"
fi

# native:package bumps NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION_CODE in .env and the endpoint
# below is written there too; put .env back afterwards.
cp .env .env.build-backup
trap 'mv .env.build-backup .env' EXIT

# Unique build number: the app re-extracts its bundled code only when the
# version or build number changes, so an install over an older build would
# otherwise keep running the old code.
sed -i.tmp "s#^NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION_CODE=.*#NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION_CODE=$(date +%s)#" .env && rm -f .env.tmp

if [ -n "${SHOP_API_URL:-}" ]; then
    if grep -q '^SHOP_API_URL=' .env; then
        sed -i.tmp "s#^SHOP_API_URL=.*#SHOP_API_URL=${SHOP_API_URL}#" .env && rm -f .env.tmp
    else
        echo "SHOP_API_URL=${SHOP_API_URL}" >> .env
    fi
fi

# NativePHP bundles the Laravel app (composer --no-dev), compiles plugins,
# runs `gradlew assembleRelease` and signs the APK with the given keystore.
php artisan native:package android \
    --build-type=release \
    --keystore="$DEBUG_KEYSTORE" \
    --keystore-password=android \
    --key-alias=androiddebugkey \
    --key-password=android \
    --no-tty

echo "APK: $PWD/nativephp/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk"
EOF

# Building Everbloom (NativePHP)

All commands run from the project root of a clean checkout, on macOS (Apple silicon).

## Toolchain used

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| macOS host PHP / Composer | PHP 8.5.12 (Homebrew), Composer 2.11.2 |
| Laravel | 13.42.0 |
| NativePHP for Mobile (`nativephp/mobile`) | 4.7.0 |
| NativePHP UI components (`nativephp/mobile-ui`) | 0.9.0 |
| NativePHP Browser plugin (`nativephp/mobile-browser`) | 1.2.1 |
| Embedded PHP runtime (downloaded by `native:install`, non-ICU) | 8.4.27 |
| Xcode / iOS SDK | Xcode 27.2 (27B52), iOS SDK 27.2 |
| CocoaPods | 1.16.2 |
| iOS Simulator runtime used for verification | iOS 26.5, iPhone 17 Pro |
| JDK | OpenJDK 21.0.6 (Android Studio JBR) |
| Gradle / AGP / Kotlin | 8.14.5 / 8.13.2 / 2.0.0 (from NativePHP's Android template) |
| Android SDK | compileSdk/targetSdk 36, minSdk 33, build-tools 36.0.0 |

Prerequisites: Xcode with an iOS platform installed, CocoaPods (`brew install cocoapods`), PHP ≥ 8.3 with the `zip`
extension and Composer (`brew install php composer`), and the Android SDK at `~/Library/Android/sdk` (or set
`ANDROID_HOME`) with a JDK 17+ on the `PATH` (or `JAVA_HOME` set).

## 1. Install dependencies

```sh
composer install
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
php artisan native:install both --no-interaction
```

`native:install` generates the native iOS and Android projects in `nativephp/` (git-ignored, regenerated on every
install) and downloads the embedded PHP runtime for both platforms.

## 2. iOS device release build (benchmarked)

Signed build (automatic signing with your team ID):

```sh
DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX scripts/build-ios.sh device
```

Without `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` the same command builds with code signing disabled (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`):

```sh
scripts/build-ios.sh device
```

Resulting app:

```
nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/NativePHP.app
```

(The executable/bundle file is named `NativePHP.app` by NativePHP's Xcode template; its display name is
`Everbloom` and its bundle identifier is `dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativephp`.)

What the script does: `php artisan native:build --release --simulated` configures the generated Xcode project
(bundle id, display name, Info.plist, plugins, icons, CocoaPods/SPM) and stages the Laravel app in release mode
(`composer install --no-dev`, optimized autoloader, maximum zip compression); then it runs
`xcodebuild -scheme NativePHP -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -destination generic/platform=iOS` (arm64).
Each build gets a unique `CFBundleVersion` (Unix time), because a NativePHP app only re-extracts its bundled code
when the version or build number changes.

## 3. Install and launch on a connected iPhone

```sh
xcrun devicectl list devices
DEVICE=<identifier from the list>
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/NativePHP.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" \
    --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"http://192.168.1.20:8787/api"}' \
    dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativephp
```

Omit `--environment-variables` to use the default endpoint `https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`.
The app reads `SHOP_API_URL` from its process environment at launch (an empty value is ignored).

## 4. iOS Simulator build

```sh
scripts/build-ios.sh simulator
```

Resulting app:

```
nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/NativePHP-simulator.app
```

Install and launch (booted simulator):

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/NativePHP-simulator.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api xcrun simctl launch booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativephp
```

Watch the readiness marker:

```sh
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'
```

## 5. Android release APK

```sh
scripts/build-android.sh
```

Resulting APK (release build, signed with the Android debug key `~/.android/debug.keystore`, created if missing):

```
nativephp/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
```

Install and launch:

```sh
adb install -r -d nativephp/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativephp/com.nativephp.mobile.ui.MainActivity
```

Endpoint: Android reads `SHOP_API_URL` at build time. Pass it to the build script, which writes it into the
bundled app's `.env` for that build only:

```sh
SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api scripts/build-android.sh
```

(Alternatively set `SHOP_API_URL=...` in `.env` before building.) Plain HTTP is allowed on both platforms. The
readiness marker goes to logcat: `adb logcat -s SHOPBENCH`.

## 6. Build modes

| Target | Mode |
|---|---|

```

install) and downloads the embedded PHP runtime for both platforms.

Signed build (automatic signing with your team ID):

```sh

```

Without `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` the same command builds with code signing disabled (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`):

```sh

```

`Everbloom` and its bundle identifier is `dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativephp`.)

(bundle id, display name, Info.plist, plugins, icons, CocoaPods/SPM) and stages the Laravel app in release mode
(`composer install --no-dev`, optimized autoloader, maximum zip compression); then it runs
`xcodebuild -scheme NativePHP -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -destination generic/platform=iOS` (arm64).
Each build gets a unique `CFBundleVersion` (Unix time), because a NativePHP app only re-extracts its bundled code
when the version or build number changes.

```sh

DEVICE=<identifier from the list>
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/NativePHP.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" \

    dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativephp

The app reads `SHOP_API_URL` from its process environment at launch (an empty value is ignored).

```sh

```

Resulting app:

```
nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/NativePHP-simulator.app
```

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted nativephp/ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/NativePHP-simulator.app

```

Watch the readiness marker:

```sh
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'
```

## 5. Android release APK

```sh
scripts/build-android.sh
```

Resulting APK (release build, signed with the Android debug key `~/.android/debug.keystore`, created if missing):

```

```

Install and launch:

```sh

No dev server is started; the app runs fully from its bundle. |
| Android | Gradle `assembleRelease` (NativePHP `native:package --build-type=release`), signed with the debug keystore; Laravel bundle in release mode. R8 minification is off (NativePHP default). |

# Notes

Everbloom built with NativePHP for Mobile v4 ("SuperNative"): the UI is native SwiftUI (iOS) / Jetpack Compose
(Android) rendered from EDGE Blade elements, driven by PHP running on the device. No web view is used.

## Architecture

- `app/NativeComponents/Shell.php` is the only native screen (`routes/mobile.php`). It owns the three tab stacks,
  the per-screen state, the in-memory cart and all handlers. Views live in `resources/views/native/`
  (`shell.blade.php`, `screens/*`, `partials/*`).
- `app/Shop/Storefront.php` sends GraphQL as plain HTTP (Laravel's HTTP client, `POST` JSON with
  `operationName`, `query`, `variables`). Each request carries the operation exactly as written in
  `resources/graphql/storefront.graphql` (a verbatim copy of `spec/storefront.graphql`) plus only the fragments it
  spreads (an unused fragment would make the document invalid).
- `app/Shop/Format.php` formats money (`$` + two decimals, no thousands separator) and appends `width` to image URLs.
- Requests run on NativePHP's background PHP lane (`AsyncTask`), so the UI never waits on the network. Responses are
  dropped if the screen has been closed or a newer request for it was sent (sort change, new search query, etc.).
- `packages/shopbench-native` is a small app-local NativePHP plugin (see Dependencies).

## Decisions where the spec is silent

- **Why one screen.** NativePHP's router has a single navigation stack. Its native tab bar keeps each tab's
  SwiftUI views, but a tab tap *replaces* the PHP screen, so a tab's screens lose their state when you switch back.
  Its tab bar also exposes no accessibility identifiers, and on iOS it is always hidden on pushed screens (the
  Collection design shows it). So `Shell` keeps the three stacks itself and renders the top screen of the active
  tab, plus a tab bar drawn with EDGE elements. Only the visible screen is rendered, so identifiers such as `back`
  or `recommendation-0` are never duplicated by hidden screens. Screens further down a stack keep their data.
  Because only the top screen is rendered, a list underneath is rebuilt when you go back; the row you tapped is
  scrolled back to the top (`auto-scroll-to`), so you return to where you were in a collection or search.
- **Consequences:** pushes and pops use no slide animation, and there is no iOS edge-swipe-back gesture. The spec
  allows no animations beyond the framework default, and the framework's default for swapping content within one
  screen is none. Android's hardware back pops the active tab's stack, and exits the app at a tab root.
- Tapping the tab you are already on does nothing (it does not pop to the root).
- **First Home load.** `Shell` is `#[Lazy]`: NativePHP paints the placeholder (the Home skeleton and tab bar)
  before `mount()` runs. `mount()` then sends the first `Home` request inline instead of on the background lane,
  because that lane only starts 0.4–3 s after launch (and on Android refuses tasks for 2.5 s). All later requests,
  including Retry, use the background lane. If the background lane refuses a task, the request runs inline.
- `SHOPBENCH home_ready` is written from `render()` in the first render where Home's loaded content (chips and
  best-seller cards) is on screen, once per process. It goes through the plugin's `Shopbench.Log` bridge function
  (`NSLog` on iOS, `Log.i("SHOPBENCH", …)` on Android).
- **Endpoint:** iOS uses `getenv('SHOP_API_URL')` from the process environment (devicectl / simctl). Android, and
  iOS without the variable, use `SHOP_API_URL` from the bundled `.env` (set at build time). Otherwise the default
  mock.shop endpoint. HTTP timeouts: 8 s connect, 20 s total.
- **Collection grid:** a `<native:list>` (SwiftUI `List` / Compose `LazyColumn`, both lazy) whose rows hold two cards.
  It is NativePHP's lazy list with an end-reached callback; `<native:lazy-grid>` has none. Pagination triggers
  when a row within 3 rows of the end is built, about one screen ahead. Column gap 12, row gap 20 as designed.
  Search results use the same list with a 6-row buffer.
- **Sort chips** in a horizontally scrolling row (they don't fit on one 390 pt line, as in the design).
- **Product price colour:** when the selected variant has a higher compare-at price, the price uses the `sale`
  colour (like the cards) with the compare-at price struck through. Search rows and recommendation cards show only
  the price, as drawn in the design. Best-seller and collection-grid cards use the sale treatment as specified.
- **Option selection:** the variant whose `selectedOptions` equal the current selection with the tapped value
  swapped in. If none matches exactly, the first variant that has the tapped value. Option pills wrap onto more
  lines if there are many.
- **Add to cart** is ignored, and the button drawn at 50 % opacity, while any cart request is in flight. The app
  switches to the Cart tab when the response has no `userErrors`. With `userErrors`, the cart is still replaced
  and the first message is shown in an alert. A network failure shows the alert "Couldn’t add to cart".
- **Cart stepper:** taps are ignored while a cart request is in flight (the stepper dims), so quantities never
  race. A failed update shows an alert.
- **Pagination failure** (a later page of a collection or search): the loading row disappears and scrolling to
  the end again retries. A first-page failure shows the error state with Retry.
- **Empty search field:** the hint text; clearing the field cancels any outstanding query. The query is trimmed.
- **Product screen while loading/failed:** round back button, then a spinner or the error state.
- Collection title is shown from the Home data immediately and replaced by the API title when it loads.
- **"See all"** link next to "Collections" in the design: not implemented. The spec doesn't list it and gives it
  no destination.
- **Colours** come from `config/native-ui.php` theme tokens matching `Tokens.dc.html`. The banner caption scrim
  is `text` at 72 % opacity. The app is pinned to light appearance (`NATIVEPHP_APPEARANCE=light`): no dark mode.
- **Icons:** the design's home, search, cart and back SVGs (plus the stepper's minus and plus) are in
  `resources/icons/`. NativePHP compiles them into vector template images (iOS asset catalog, Android
  VectorDrawable).
- **Plain white launch screen:** `public/splash.png` / `splash-dark.png` are plain white, replacing NativePHP's
  default logo splash. App icon: NativePHP's default (no custom icon was made).
- **Portrait iPhone only** (`ipad => false`, portrait orientation in `config/nativephp.php`).
- `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone = true` and `NSAppTransportSecurity` (`NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`,
  `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`) are set through `config('nativephp.permissions')`, which NativePHP merges into
  Info.plist. Android cleartext is enabled by the plugin's `network_security_config.xml`.
- **Builds use a unique build number** (Unix time) because NativePHP only re-extracts the bundled app when the
  version or build number changes. `NATIVEPHP_APP_VERSION` is `1.0.0`; `DEBUG` would re-extract on every launch.
- `.env.example` turns logging off (`LOG_CHANNEL=null`) and uses array session/cache drivers, so nothing is
  persisted (NativePHP still creates its SQLite file, but the app stores nothing in it).

## Dependencies added

| Dependency | Why |
|---|---|
| `nativephp/mobile` 4.7.0 | The framework (required). |
| `nativephp/mobile-ui` 0.9.0 | NativePHP's own EDGE element renderers (column, text, image, list, pager…). Core has no renderers without it. |
| `nativephp/mobile-browser` 1.2.x | In-app browser (SFSafariViewController / Custom Tabs) for Check out. NativePHP core has no browser API. |
| `shopbench/native` (local, `packages/shopbench-native`) | App-local NativePHP plugin: the `Shopbench.Log` bridge function (NativePHP has no way for PHP to write to the iOS unified log) and the Android `network_security_config.xml` allowing cleartext (NativePHP's release config forbids it). |
| `laravel/framework` | NativePHP apps are Laravel apps (from the official starter). |
| `phpunit/phpunit` (dev only) | Needed by NativePHP's in-process component test harness (`Native::test()`), which I used during development. Not shipped: release bundles are built with `composer --no-dev`. |

Development-only tooling (not in the project): the AXe CLI was used to drive the iOS Simulator by accessibility
identifier during verification.

## Not met / caveats

- **Framework logging in release builds:** NativePHP's iOS shell itself calls `NSLog` (e.g. `[NativePHP] Deferred
  initialization starting`, `AsyncTaskExecutor: started`) in release builds. The app adds only the single
  `SHOPBENCH home_ready` line. Removing the framework's lines would mean modifying NativePHP, which the spec forbids.
- **NativePHP starts its queue worker and async-task pool** (extra PHP interpreters) at launch on every app. This
  isn't configurable without modifying the framework.
- **Native push/pop animations and the edge-swipe-back gesture are absent** (see "Why one screen").
- **Simulator build configuration:** NativePHP's simulator scheme always compiles Xcode's Debug configuration. The
  bundled PHP app is in release mode (see BUILD.md).
- **No product in the mock catalog has variants with different prices,** so the price update on variant change
  could only be checked in code and by the label and pill state changing on the simulator.
- **Accessibility element types:** identifiers come from NativePHP's `ref` attribute (iOS
  `accessibilityIdentifier`, Android `testTag` exposed as resource-id). Pressables are buttons. The
  `cart-badge` and `cart-subtotal` elements are generic elements whose accessibility label is the displayed value.
  Lists and scroll views expose their identifier on the scrolling container.

content.text:
The Everbloom app is built with NativePHP v4 (native SwiftUI/Compose, no web view), and every Done item checks out except the signed iOS device build. That one can't run on this Mac because there's no Apple developer account for the team (Xcode stops at "No Account for Team"). The unsigned device build (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) succeeds.

**What I verified**
- **Clean checkout:** I copied the project without git-ignored files and ran the `BUILD.md` commands. The iOS device build (unsigned, arm64 Release), the iOS Simulator build and the Android release APK all succeeded.
- **iOS Simulator flows** all work: Home; a collection scrolled to its last product (all 84); all four sorts; search with infinite scroll (81 results for "jacket"); options; a recommendation opening another product; add to cart switching to Cart with the badge; the stepper and subtotal; quantity 0 showing the empty cart; Check out opening the in-app browser.
- **Option switching** is only partly verified. No product in the mock catalog has variants with different prices, so I could only confirm the label and pill selection change; the price update is checked in code.
- **Error state:** pointing `SHOP_API_URL` at a dead local server shows the error screen. Retry loads Home once the server is up.
- **Log marker:** `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears once per launch in the simulator log (and in Android logcat). On a warm launch it arrives about 1.8 s after launch.
- **Android emulator:** the APK launches and Home loads.
- **Accessibility IDs:** all are present in the iOS accessibility tree (checked with the AXe CLI, a dev-only tool). `cart-badge` and `cart-subtotal` come through as generic elements whose label is the displayed value.

**Deviations from the spec (all recorded in `NOTES.md`)**
- **No native push/pop animation or iOS swipe-back.** NativePHP's built-in tabs don't keep each tab's screens when you switch, expose no accessibility IDs, and on iOS hide the tab bar on every pushed screen. So the whole app is one screen that manages the three tab stacks itself and draws its own tab bar. Going back returns you to the row you tapped in a collection or search.
- **Extra framework logging.** NativePHP itself writes `[NativePHP] …` lines to the iOS log in release builds, and starts a queue worker and async pool at launch. Neither can be changed without modifying NativePHP. The app adds only the `home_ready` line.
- **The Simulator build uses Xcode's Debug configuration.** That's the only option NativePHP's simulator scheme offers; the bundled app code is in release mode.
- **Not implemented: the "See all" link** next to Collections in the design. The spec doesn't list it and gives it no destination.
- **Android scrim colour:** the banner caption scrim showed the wrong colour on Android. I fixed it and confirmed it on the clean Android build only; the iOS app was last built before the fix.

**Added beyond the framework itself**
- **`nativephp/mobile-browser`:** the in-app browser for Check out.
- **`packages/shopbench-native`:** a small local plugin. It provides the NSLog/logcat bridge for the log marker and the Android setting that allows plain HTTP.
- **`phpunit/phpunit` (dev only):** needed by NativePHP's in-process component test harness; not shipped in release bundles.

Build commands, output paths, build modes and toolchain versions are in `BUILD.md`. The builds are wrapped in `scripts/build-ios.sh` and `scripts/build-android.sh`.
